definition_zh: 敢；敢于；激（某人做某事）；胆量；挑战
definition_en: to be brave enough to do something; to challenge someone to do it
core_image: 站在跳水板最前端深吸一口气
scene: 班级才艺秀报名截止前，同桌笑着看我，我握紧了话筒报名唱歌。 My friends dared me to sing on the stage, and I said yes.
sceneCN: 这里 dare 是「激；怂恿」（第 2 个义项：用挑战口气促使某人做某事）；句意是朋友们激我上台唱歌，我答应了。

derivatives.zh: 由 dare 加 -ing 构成，义为「大胆的；勇敢的」
由 daring 加 -ly 构成，义为「大胆地」

senses.title: Be brave enough
senses.definition: to have enough courage to do something difficult or frightening
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的勇气去做困难或可怕的事
senses.example: She did not dare to touch the snake at the science show.
senses.exampleCN: 在科普展上她不敢碰那条蛇。
senses.why: Standing at the edge with the jump ahead, courage is the only push left.
senses.whyCN: 站在跳板边缘、面前就是纵身一跃时，剩下的推力只有勇气。

senses.title: Challenge somebody to do something
senses.definition: to tell someone they should do something difficult, to make them try
senses.definitionCN: 用话语刺激别人去做难事，促使他尝试
senses.example: They dared him to jump from the low wall, and he refused.
senses.exampleCN: 他们激他从矮墙上跳下去，他拒绝了。
senses.why: Bravery can be lent by others: a dare hands the challenge across.
senses.whyCN: 勇气也可以被别人「借」给你：一句 dare 把挑战递了过去。

senses.title: A bold challenge
senses.definition: an act of daring someone; boldness
senses.definitionCN: 激将的行为；大胆
senses.example: Eating the lemon whole was just a dare at lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 整个吞下柠檬不过是午餐时的一个打赌挑战。
senses.why: The challenge itself gets the name of the verb that throws it.
senses.whyCN: 挑战本身便借用了抛出它的动词之名。

intro.en: Dare is one of the oldest courage words in English.
intro.cn: dare 是英语中最古老的「勇气」词汇之一。

items.en: durran meant to have courage; the past tense was dorste.
items.cn: 古英语 durran 意为有勇气，过去式是 dorste。

items.en: It comes from a Germanic verb family about boldness, shared with related German words.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼语系中关于「大胆」的动词家族，与德语相关词同源。

items.en: Forms settled into dare and durst, the old past tense.
items.cn: 形式定型为 dare 与旧式过去式 durst。

items.en: The challenging sense grew: to dare someone meant to hand them a bold test.
items.cn: 「激将」义发展起来：dare someone 即把大胆的考验抛给对方。

items.en: Today dare covers courage, challenges and the famous How dare you.
items.cn: 如今 dare 涵盖勇气、挑战以及那句著名的 How dare you。

note.en: These words share the old Germanic root or describe courage.
note.cn: 这些词与古老的日耳曼词根同源，或描述勇气。

normal.en: daring is the adjective: a daring jump.
normal.cn: 形容词是 daring：a daring jump（大胆的一跃）。

normal.en: Don't you dare! warns someone not to try.

definition_zh: 睡着的；麻木的
definition_en: in a state of sleep, or without feeling in a part of the body
core_image: 婴儿在隔壁房间闭着眼睛安睡
scene: 隔壁房间里，婴儿闭着眼睛安静地睡着。 The baby is asleep in the next room.
sceneCN: 这里 asleep 是「睡着的」（第 1 个义项：处于睡眠状态）；句意为婴儿在隔壁房间睡着了。

derivatives.zh: 睡觉
困倦的

senses.title: In sleep
senses.definition: in a state of sleep
senses.definitionCN: 处在睡眠的状态
senses.example: The baby is asleep in the next room.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿在隔壁房间睡着了。
senses.why: The prefix marks being inside a state, and sleep is that state, so sleeping is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 前缀标记处在某种状态，sleep 就是那种状态，所以睡着是第一义。

senses.title: Without feeling
senses.definition: numb and unable to feel, often after pressure
senses.definitionCN: 麻木、感觉不到，常因受压而起
senses.example: My foot is asleep after sitting so long.
senses.exampleCN: 坐得太久，我的脚麻了。
senses.why: A limb that has lost feeling seems shut in its own stillness, so the sleeping picture is borrowed.
senses.whyCN: 失去感觉的肢体像被关在自己的静止里，于是借用了「睡着」的画面。

intro.en: The recorded history of asleep is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 asleep 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Slæp meant sleep, the state of rest.
items.cn: slæp 意为睡眠，即休息的状态。

items.en: The prefix a- meant on or in.
items.cn: 前缀 a- 意为在……之上或之中。

items.en: English joined the prefix and the noun into asleep.
items.cn: 英语把前缀与名词合成 asleep。

items.en: The word first described a person held in sleep.
items.cn: 这个词最初形容处在睡眠中的人。

items.en: Today it also describes a limb without feeling.
items.cn: 今天它也形容失去感觉的肢体。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The noun and verb for resting with eyes closed.
entries.definitionCN: 表示闭眼休息的名词与动词。

entries.definition: The adjective for feeling the need to sleep.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指感到困倦。

entries.definition: The form used before a noun for a sleeping person.
entries.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指睡着的。

entries.definition: It stands before a noun rather than after be.
entries.definitionCN: 多放在名词前，而非 be 之后。

entries.definition: It is the opposite state, with eyes open.
entries.definitionCN: 相反的状态，眼睛睁着。

entries.definition: It names the loss of feeling directly.
entries.definitionCN: 直接指失去感觉。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: a- means in and sleep is the state: asleep is being held inside sleep.
normal.cn: a- 表示在……之中，sleep 是状态：asleep 就是被睡眠包住。

normal.en: The same family also gives sleep and sleepy.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 sleep 与 sleepy。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase fall asleep.

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of asleep in order.

definition_en: a device of connected parts that performs work; also a computer or an organised system, and to cut or shape with a machine tool

sceneCN: 这里 machine 指由部件组成并做功的装置（第 1 个义项：机器这一装置）；句意：这台机器把轴削到与要求尺寸相差不到一根头发。

senses.title: A device that performs work
senses.definition: an assembly of connected parts that uses power to carry out a task
senses.definitionCN: 由相连部件构成、使用动力完成任务的组合体
senses.example: The machine lifts the load with a single lever.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器只用一个手柄就抬起货物。
senses.why: the Greek noun named any contrivance, so the first sense is the broad one of a built device.
senses.whyCN: 希腊名词原指任何巧妙装置，因此第一个义项就是「人造装置」这一宽泛含义。

senses.title: A computer
senses.definition: the computing hardware that executes stored instructions
senses.definitionCN: 执行已存指令的计算硬件
senses.example: The machine rebooted before the backup finished.
senses.exampleCN: 备份还没完成，机器就重启了。
senses.why: computers became the most common machine in daily life, and speakers shortened the name.
senses.whyCN: 计算机成了日常最常见的机器，说话者就把名称缩短了。

senses.title: A household or workshop appliance
senses.definition: a named device for one task, as in a washing or sewing machine
senses.definitionCN: 为单一任务命名的装置，如洗衣机或缝纫机
senses.example: The sewing machine has outlived three owners.
senses.exampleCN: 那台缝纫机已经比三位主人活得都久。
senses.why: a device is named by its task plus this general word, which is how the compound names spread.
senses.whyCN: 装置以「任务＋这个总称」命名，这类复合名称就是这样扩散的。

senses.title: A machine tool
senses.definition: a powered tool that cuts or shapes metal and other materials
senses.definitionCN: 切削或成型金属等材料的动力工具
senses.example: The new machine holds a tolerance of a hundredth of a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 这台新机床能保持百分之一毫米的公差。
senses.why: in a workshop, the general word often means the tool that makes other parts.
senses.whyCN: 在车间里，这个总称常指制造其他零件的工具。

senses.title: To cut or shape by machine
senses.definition: to remove material or form a part with a powered tool
senses.definitionCN: 用动力工具去除材料或成型零件
senses.example: They machined the block in two passes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们分两道工序加工了那块坯料。
senses.why: the noun became a verb the moment the tool's action needed a name.
senses.whyCN: 当工具的动作需要一个名称时，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: A political organisation
senses.definition: the permanent staff and structure that win elections or hold power
senses.definitionCN: 赢得选举或维持权力的常设人员与结构
senses.example: The party machine decided the candidate before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 政党机器在投票之前就决定了候选人。
senses.why: an organisation that runs without sentiment is described by the most impersonal noun available.
senses.whyCN: 不带感情运转的组织，就用最非人格的名词来描述。

senses.title: An impersonal system of rule
senses.definition: the administrative apparatus of a state or large institution
senses.definitionCN: 国家或大型机构的行政装置
senses.example: The state machine ground down every small request.
senses.exampleCN: 国家机器把每一个小请求都磨掉了。
senses.why: the image of interlocking parts describes bureaucracy better than any abstract word.
senses.whyCN: 「咬合的部件」这一意象，比任何抽象词都更能描述官僚体系。

senses.title: A person who acts automatically
senses.definition: a person treated as incapable of independent thought
senses.definitionCN: 被视为无法独立思考的人
senses.example: They turned him into a machine that answered tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把他变成一台只回答工单的机器。
senses.why: calling a person a machine denies judgement, which is the insult the word carries here.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫作机器就是否认其判断力，这正是这个词在此处的贬义。

senses.title: Automated by computation
senses.definition: used before a noun for processes carried out by computers
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指由计算机完成的过程
senses.example: Machine translation improved, but it still misses tone.
senses.exampleCN: 机器翻译进步了，却仍抓不住语气。
senses.why: as a modifier, the word marks the shift from human to computed action.
senses.whyCN: 作修饰语时，这个词标记从人工到计算动作的转移。

senses.title: The power unit of a vehicle
senses.definition: the engine and its housing in a boat, train or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 船、火车或车辆中的发动机及其外壳
senses.example: The fire machine kept its pump running for nine hours.
senses.exampleCN: 消防车的泵持续运转了九个小时。
senses.why: early industrial English called a powered vehicle a machine, and the usage survives in a few names.
senses.whyCN: 早期工业英语把动力车辆叫作 machine，这种用法在少数名称里留存下来。

intro.en: Machine came from Greek mekhane through Latin machina and French. It meant any contrivance long before it meant a powered device, and its computing and organisational senses are later extensions.
intro.cn: machine 经拉丁语 machina 与法语来自希腊语 mekhane。它很久以前指任何巧妙装置，之后才指动力装置；计算机义与组织义是更晚的延伸。

items.en: Greek mekhane named a device, especially a stage crane or a siege engine, and also a means or expedient.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置，尤指舞台吊机或攻城器械，也指手段与办法。

items.en: Latin machina meant a structure, scaffold or engine, and the phrase deus ex machina came from the stage crane.
items.cn: 拉丁语 machina 指结构、脚手架或器械，短语 deus ex machina 就来自舞台吊机。

items.en: French machine entered English in the seventeenth century and covered any constructed device, not only powered ones.
items.cn: 法语 machine 在十七世纪进入英语，指任何建造出来的装置，而不只是动力装置。

items.en: Steam and factory work narrowed machine toward devices with moving parts driven by power.
items.cn: 蒸汽与工厂作业把 machine 收窄为由动力驱动、带运动部件的装置。

items.en: The twentieth century added the computer and the party machine, both built on the image of parts working together.
items.cn: 二十世纪加上计算机与政党机器两义，二者都建立在「部件协同运转」的意象上。

items.en: Machining arose in workshops as the verb for what a machine tool does to metal.
items.cn: machining 在车间里产生，指机床对金属所做的加工。

note.en: The first group is the machine family in other shapes; the second group is the neighbouring words for devices and systems.
note.cn: 第一组是 machine 词族的其他形态；第二组是装置与体系的相邻说法。

entries.definition: Machines as a mass; one machine is countable, machinery is not.
entries.definitionCN: 指机器的整体；一台机器可数，machinery 不可数。

entries.definition: A person who operates or makes machines; the noun names the equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 指操作或制造机器的人；名词指设备。

entries.definition: A person who repairs machines; a machine is the thing repaired.
entries.definitionCN: 指修理机器的人；machine 是被修的东西。

entries.definition: The set of parts that produces a motion; a machine contains one or more mechanisms.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生运动的那组部件；一台机器包含一个或多个机构。

entries.definition: Any constructed thing made for a purpose, often small; a machine usually has moving parts and power.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的造的任何东西，常指小型；machine 通常有运动部件与动力。

entries.definition: A machine that converts energy into motion; it is a part of many machines.
entries.definitionCN: 把能量转成运动的机器；它是许多机器的一个部件。

entries.definition: An implement a person holds and guides; a machine supplies its own motion.
entries.definitionCN: 由人握持与引导的器具；machine 自己提供运动。

entries.definition: A set of equipment working as one, often for an experiment or an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体工作的一整套设备，常用于实验或机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Greek source and the real noun-verb pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实希腊语来源与真实名词动词成对关系。

normal.en: Mekhane meant a stage crane, so a machine is first a thing that lifts and moves.
normal.cn: mekhane 原指舞台吊机，所以 machine 首先是能吊起与移动东西的装置。

normal.en: The verb forms are regular: machines, machined, machined, machining.
normal.cn: 动词形式规则：machines、machined、machined、machining。

normal.en: Task names build on it: washing machine, sewing machine, machine tool.
normal.cn: 任务名称在它之上构成：洗衣机、缝纫机、机床。

normal.en: The computing sense is simply the shortened name of the most common machine.
normal.cn: 计算机义不过是「最常用机器」的简称。

normal.en: Two objects split the verb: machine a part, machine a surface.
normal.cn: 两类宾语分开动词：加工一个零件，加工一个表面。

abstract.en: Picture a crane on a stage lowering a god who is only a painted board.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上的吊机放下一个神，而那神不过是一块画板。

abstract.en: Picture a lathe turning a shaft until the metal is exactly the size of an idea.
abstract.cn: 想象车床削一根轴，直到金属恰好等于一个想法的尺寸。

abstract.en: Picture an office where every request disappears into a slot and comes out stamped.
abstract.cn: 想象一间办公室，每个请求都落进一个槽口，再盖着章出来。

examples.en: The machine does the lifting, but a person still chooses where.
examples.cn: 机器负责起吊，但选择吊到哪里仍由人决定。

examples.en: They machined the replacement part overnight.
examples.cn: 他们连夜加工了那只替换零件。

examples.en: The party machine had chosen the nominee months earlier.
examples.cn: 政党机器几个月前就已定下候选人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马（ma）身（chine）」——马拉着的一副身架，就是最早干活的机器

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置、舞台吊机」→ 拉丁 machina「结构、器械」→ 法语 machine → 英语 machine；先泛指装置，工业时代收窄为动力装置，二十世纪扩展出计算机与组织体系义，动词指机床加工。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses run from the general device to the computer, the appliance, the machine tool, the verb, the party machine, the state apparatus, the dehumanised person, computed processes and the vehicle's power unit.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从泛指的装置出发，经过计算机、家用器具、机床、动词用法、政党机器、国家机器、被机械化的人、计算化流程，最后到车辆动力机组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lathe holding a metal shaft while a cutter advances and curls off chips.
core.cn: 核心意象：车床夹着一段金属轴，刀头推进，铁屑卷曲落下。

branches.en: DEVICES: any working assembly, and the named appliance built on that pattern.
branches.cn: 装置：任何做功的组合体，以及按此模式命名的器具。

branches.en: COMPUTATION: the computer itself, and processes carried out by computed action.
branches.cn: 计算：计算机本身，以及由计算动作完成的过程。

branches.en: TOOL AND ACTION: the machine tool, and the verb for what it does to metal.
branches.cn: 工具与动作：机床，以及它对金属所做加工的动词。

branches.en: ORGANISED POWER: the party machine, and the administrative apparatus of a state.
branches.cn: 组织化的权力：政党机器，以及国家的行政装置。

branches.en: THE MECHANICAL FIGURE: a person reduced to a machine, and a vehicle's engine unit.
branches.cn: 机械化的形象：被降为机器的人，以及车辆的动力机组。

intro.en: Machine is a borrowed noun with no living affix; its family adds -ery, -ist, -ing and compound forms.
intro.cn: machine 是借入名词，本身没有能产的词缀；其词族另加 -ery、-ist、-ing 与复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin machina is the direct source of the French and English forms; the Greek noun mekhane stands behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 machina 是法语与英语形式的直接来源，其背后是希腊名词 mekhane。

items.example: The Greek noun carries both the machine and the trick.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词兼有「机器」与「计策」两面。

items.example: Latin widened the noun to any built structure.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个名词扩大到任何建造的结构。

items.meaning: device; to cut with a tool
items.example: English uses the same form for the object and the action.
items.exampleCN: 英语用同一形式指对象与动作。

items.example: The ending produces the uncountable collective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾产生不可数的集合名词。

items.example: The ending names the cutting work itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指切削工作本身。

items.example: The ending marks what a device can read or do.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记装置能读或能做的事。

items.example: The ending names one arrangement of moving parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指一套运动部件的组合。

definition_zh: 宣布；公布；播报；预示
definition_en: to tell people about a piece of news in a public or formal way
core_image: 校长站在礼堂台上向全校宣布成绩
scene: 礼堂里，校长站在台上向全校师生宣布成绩。 The head teacher announced the exam results.
sceneCN: 这里 announced 是「宣布」（第 1 个义项：公开正式告知）；句意为校长宣布了考试成绩。

derivatives.zh: 公告；通知
播音员
已宣布的

senses.title: To announce publicly
senses.definition: to tell a piece of news to people in a public or formal way
senses.definitionCN: 以公开或正式的方式把消息告诉众人
senses.example: The head teacher announced the exam results.
senses.exampleCN: 校长宣布了考试成绩。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to report, and reporting news to a whole crowd is the first use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为报告，把消息报告给整个人群就是第一义。

senses.title: To read out on air
senses.definition: to read out information on radio or television
senses.definitionCN: 在广播或电视上念出信息
senses.example: The radio announced the winner at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 电台在中午播报了获胜者。
senses.why: A voice carrying news to many listeners repeats the old report, now through a microphone.
senses.whyCN: 声音把消息传给许多听众，重复了古老的「报告」，只是改用麦克风。

senses.title: To show something is coming
senses.definition: to make it clear that something is about to happen
senses.definitionCN: 清楚表明某事即将发生
senses.example: Dark clouds announced the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 乌云预示了暴风雨。
senses.why: When a sign speaks of what comes next, the public telling becomes a silent warning.
senses.whyCN: 当迹象说出了接下来要发生的事，公开告知就变成无声的预警。

intro.en: The recorded history of announce is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 announce 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Nuntiare meant to report or to bring news.
items.cn: nuntiare 意为报告或带来消息。

items.en: Nuntius meant a messenger who carried words.
items.cn: nuntius 意为传递话语的信使。

items.en: French shaped the verb into anoncer, to make known.
items.cn: 法语把这个动词变成 anoncer，意为使人知道。

items.en: English borrowed it for making news public.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪借入它，指把消息公开。

items.en: Today it covers speeches, broadcasts and warning signs.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖演讲、广播与预警迹象。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The third person form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数形式。

entries.definition: The past form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式。

entries.definition: The noun for a public notice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指公开的通知。

entries.definition: It is often formal and official.
entries.definitionCN: 通常正式而官方。

entries.definition: It stresses telling what has happened.
entries.definitionCN: 强调讲述发生的事。

entries.definition: It stresses sending news to many listeners.
entries.definitionCN: 强调把消息传给众多听众。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: ad- means to and nuntius means a messenger: to announce is to send a message to people.
normal.cn: ad- 表示向，nuntius 表示信使：announce 就是把消息送给众人。

normal.en: The same family also gives announcement and announcer.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 announcement 与 announcer。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase announce the news.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「宣布消息」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of announce in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 announce 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: to tell people about a piece of news in a public or formal way.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「宣布」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a head teacher announcing results to the whole school from a hall stage.
abstract.cn: 想象校长站在礼堂台上向全校宣布成绩。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: The head teacher announced the exam results.
examples.cn: 校长宣布了考试成绩。

examples.cn: 电台在中午播报了获胜者。

examples.en: Dark clouds announced the storm.
examples.cn: 乌云预示了暴风雨。

root: announce 来自拉丁语 nuntiare「报告」，与 nuntius「信使」同源，经法语 anoncer 进入英语；十五世纪指把消息公开，今天涵盖演讲、广播与预警迹象。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of announce grows from one core image: a head teacher announcing results to the whole school from a hall stage.
sensesIntro.cn: announce 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：校长站在礼堂台上向全校宣布成绩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a head teacher announcing results to the whole school from a hall stage
core.cn: 核心意象：校长站在礼堂台上向全校宣布成绩

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: To announce publicly.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：公开宣布。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: To read out on air.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：播报。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: To announce publicly / To read out on air.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：公开宣布、播报。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: To show something is coming.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：预示。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 03 covers the outer edge of the meaning: To announce publicly / To show something is coming.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖意义的边缘：公开宣布、预示。

intro.cn: announce 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

definition_zh: 首都；资本；大写字母；首要的
definition_en: the city where a government sits, money used in business, an uppercase letter, or something chief and most important
core_image: 一座城市的中心矗立着政府大楼，一切从「头」开始
scene: 地理课上，老师指着地图让学生找出各国的首都。 In geography class the teacher asked us to point at each capital on the map.
sceneCN: 这里 capital 是「首都」（第 1 个义项：政府所在的城市）；句意为地理课上找各国首都。

derivatives.zh: 由 capital 加 -ism 构成，义为「资本主义」
由 capital 加 -ize 构成，义为「把…大写；利用」
同根词，义为「队长；船长」

senses.title: The head city of a country
senses.definition: the city where the government of a country or region sits
senses.definitionCN: 一国或一地区政府所在的城市
senses.example: Paris is the capital of France.
senses.exampleCN: 巴黎是法国的首都。
senses.why: The head city is the head of the country, so caput names it directly.
senses.whyCN: 一国之首即「头城」，caput 直接命名了它。

senses.title: Money used to make more money
senses.definition: money or assets used to start or grow a business
senses.definitionCN: 用于创办或扩大生意的资金
senses.example: They raised capital for the new factory.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为建新厂筹集了资本。
senses.why: Wealth is the head of an enterprise, the source from which everything grows.
senses.whyCN: 财富是企业的「头」，一切由此生长。

senses.title: Uppercase letters
senses.definition: letters written in their large form, used at the start of names and sentences
senses.definitionCN: 字母的大写形式，用于句首与专名
senses.example: Write your name in capital letters.
senses.exampleCN: 用大写字母写你的名字。
senses.why: The big letter is the head letter of the alphabet's shape family.
senses.whyCN: 大写字母是字母「形族」中的大头。

senses.title: Chief and first in importance
senses.definition: first in importance, or excellent in informal British use
senses.definitionCN: 最重要的，或英式口语中的「极好」
senses.example: Safety is a capital concern in the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 安全是实验室的首要问题。
senses.why: What stands at the head of the list is what matters most.
senses.whyCN: 排在最前、居于首位的东西最为要紧。

intro.en: Capital grows entirely from Latin caput, the head, branching into cities, money and letters.
intro.cn: capital 完全由拉丁语 caput（头）生长出城市、金钱与字母诸义。

items.en: Caput meant head, and also the head or top of anything.
items.cn: caput 意为头，也指事物的顶端。

items.en: Capitalis meant of the head, hence chief or principal.
items.cn: 形容词 capitalis 意为「属于头的」，引申为首要的。

items.en: Old French passed capitalis on as capital with the same chief sense.
items.cn: 古法语将 capitalis 传为 capital，保留首要之义。

items.en: Middle English used capital for chief, then for the head city and wealth.
items.cn: 中古英语先取「首要」义，再派生首都与资本义。

items.en: Modern English added the uppercase letter and the legal sense of life-taking.
items.cn: 现代英语又添大写字母义及涉死罪的用法。

note.en: The first group collects same-root head words; the second collects city-and-money neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组收同根「头」族词，第二组收城市与金钱类近义词。

entries.definition: The leader of a team or ship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「队长；船长」，与 capital 同根。

entries.definition: A section of a book.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「章节」，古义为「文章之头」，同根。

entries.definition: Farm animals, once meant property.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「牲口」，古义「财产」，与 capital 同源。

entries.definition: Money kept for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「资金」，与资本义相近。

entries.definition: A very large chief city.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大都会」，与首都义相邻。

entries.definition: Most important.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「首要的」，与 capital 形容词义相近。

normalIntro.en: Remember capital through the head root family.
normalIntro.cn: 借「头」词根族记忆 capital。

normal.en: capital is the head city of a country.
normal.cn: capital 是一国的「头城」，即首都。

normal.en: capital letters are the big head forms of letters.
normal.cn: 大写字母是字母的大头形式。

normal.en: capital funds are the head of a business.
normal.cn: 资本是企业之「头」。

normal.en: captain, chapter and cattle all share caput.
normal.cn: captain、chapter、cattle 都源自 caput。

normal.en: a capital idea is a first-rate idea.
normal.cn: a capital idea 指「绝妙的主意」。

abstract.en: Picture one tall building towering over the whole city map.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋高楼俯瞰整张城市地图。

abstract.en: See a bank vault at the head of every plan.
abstract.cn: 想象金库居于一切计划之首。

abstract.en: Watch capital A stand tallest on the page.
abstract.cn: 看字母 A 在纸面上站得最高。

examples.en: Rome was the capital of a great empire.
examples.cn: 罗马曾是一个大帝国的首都。

examples.en: The company needs capital to expand.
examples.cn: 公司需要资本来扩张。

examples.en: Names always begin with a capital letter.
examples.cn: 专有名词总是以大写字母开头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开披头」——城市张开如披风，罩住全国的「头」。

root: 拉丁语 caput（头）→ capitalis（首要的）→ 古法语 capital → 英语 capital；同根词 captain（首领）、capitate（头状的）、per capita（人均）。

sensesIntro.en: Capital spreads from the head of a country to the head of a business, an alphabet line and a list of duties.
sensesIntro.cn: capital 从「国之首」扩散到「企业之本」「字母之首」与「事项之首」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the head that leads everything below it
core.cn: 核心意象：统领其余一切的「头」

branches.cn: 书写中的大写字母

branches.cn: 权力之首要所在

intro.cn: capital 的每个义项都留着拉丁语「头」的影子。

latinIntro.en: Caput bred an adjective capitalis that English inherited whole.
latinIntro.cn: caput 派生出形容词 capitalis，被英语整体继承。

definition_zh: 也许；可能；（口语）或许吧；不确定的事
definition_en: used to say that something is possible but not certain, or to make a gentle suggestion, and informally a thing that is still undecided

scene: 两个人站在站台上，雨云压得很低，列车时刻牌迟迟不翻。 Maybe the rain will stop before we reach the station.
sceneCN: 这里 maybe 是「也许」（第 1 个义项：表示不确定的可能）；句意为也许我们到站之前雨就会停。图中可辨识物件：站台、时刻牌、压低的雨云。

pos.zh: （口语）不确定的事；悬而未决的事

与 may 同源的历史过去式，也可表示较弱的可能
maybe 的后半部分，来自古英语表示「是、存在」的动词

senses.title: Used to say something is possible but not certain
senses.definition: used when you think something is possible, without saying that it is certain
senses.definitionCN: 在你认为某事有可能、但不确定时使用
senses.example: Maybe the rain will stop before we reach the station.
senses.exampleCN: 也许我们到站之前雨就会停。
senses.why: The word is may plus be: a compressed sentence saying it may be so, with the doubt of may kept inside.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 may 加 be，把一个意为「或许如此」的句子压缩起来，may 那点不确定感也留在里面。

senses.title: Used to make a gentle suggestion
senses.definition: used in speech to suggest a course of action without sounding like an order
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来提出某个做法，又不像在下命令
senses.example: Maybe we should call her before we drive over.
senses.exampleCN: 也许我们该在开车过去之前给她打个电话。
senses.why: A suggestion phrased with maybe leaves the decision open, so the same doubt becomes a polite way of proposing.
senses.whyCN: 用 maybe 提出的建议把决定权留开，于是同一份不确定就变成了客气地提议。

senses.title: A hesitant answer that agrees without promising
senses.definition: used alone as an answer that neither accepts nor refuses
senses.definitionCN: 单独用作回答，既不答应也不拒绝
senses.example: Will you come to the reunion? Maybe.
senses.exampleCN: 你会来聚会吗？或许吧。
senses.why: Because maybe marks an open possibility, a bare maybe as an answer lets the speaker stay uncommitted.
senses.whyCN: 因为 maybe 标出的是一种开放的可能，单独用它作答，说话人就不必作出承诺。

senses.title: Something that is still undecided
senses.definition: an informal noun for a plan or result that is not settled yet
senses.definitionCN: 非正式的名词，指尚未定下来的计划或结果
senses.example: The trip is still a maybe until the tickets are booked.
senses.exampleCN: 在机票订好之前，这趟旅行还说不准。
senses.why: Once maybe names a possibility, it can be turned into a noun for the thing that sits in that doubtful state.
senses.whyCN: 既然 maybe 指的是一种可能性，它就能被当作名词，指处在那种不确定状态里的事情。

intro.en: Maybe is an English compound rather than a borrowed word: may came from an Old English verb of ability, be from the verb of existence, and the two were written as one word in Middle English.
intro.cn: maybe 是英语本土的复合词，不是借词：may 来自古英语表示「能够」的动词，be 是表示存在的动词，两者在中古英语时期合并成一个词。

items.en: Magan meant to be able, and its present stem supplied may as the word for possibility.
items.cn: magan 意为「能够」，它的现在时词干提供了表示可能性的 may。

items.en: Beon meant to be or to exist, and it is the source of modern be in all its irregular forms.
items.cn: beon 意为「是、存在」，是现代 be 及其各种不规则形式的来源。

items.en: The two words stood side by side as may be, a clause meaning it may be so.
items.cn: 这两个词在中古英语中并排出现，写作 may be，是一个意为「或许如此」的小句。

items.en: By the late medieval period the pair was written as one word and used like an adverb.
items.cn: 到中古英语后期，这一对已被写成一个词，并像副词一样使用。

items.en: Modern English uses maybe freely in speech and informal writing, beside perhaps in more formal styles.
items.cn: 现代英语在口语和非正式写作中自由使用 maybe，较正式文体则常用 perhaps。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the parts and close neighbours of the compound; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of possibility.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的组成部分与近邻；近义组收其他表示可能性的副词。

entries.definition: The modal verb meaning can or possibly will, the front half of maybe.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，意为「可以」或「可能」，是 maybe 的前半部分。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to exist or to be, the back half of maybe.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「是、存在」的动词，是 maybe 的后半部分。

entries.definition: The past form of may, also used for weaker possibility.
entries.definitionCN: may 的过去式，也用来表示较弱的可能性。

entries.definition: A verb phrase meaning it is possible that it is, written as two words.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，意为「可能是」，写作两个词。

entries.definition: A more formal adverb for possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 表示可能性的较正式副词。

entries.definition: An adverb saying that something could happen or be true.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事可能发生或属实的副词。

entries.definition: An adverb saying something is likely, stronger than maybe.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事很可能，语气比 maybe 强。

entries.definition: Used when you suppose something is true from the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 根据证据推断某事属实时使用。

normalIntro.en: The word is two short verbs fused, and its meaning is the doubt that may brings to the plain verb be.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由两个短动词熔合而成，意思就是 may 带给 be 的那点不确定。

normal.en: Maybe is may plus be, so the word literally contains the sentence it may be.
normal.cn: maybe 是 may 加 be，字面上就装着「it may be」这句话。

normal.en: May started as an Old English verb of ability, which is why maybe carries possibility rather than certainty.
normal.cn: may 起初是古英语中表示能力的动词，所以 maybe 带的是可能而非确定。

normal.en: Written as two words, may be is a verb phrase; written as one, maybe is an adverb.
normal.cn: 写成两个词时 may be 是动词短语，写成一个词时 maybe 是副词。

normal.en: Maybe not and maybe so are the two easiest pairs to remember, one closing and one opening the possibility.
normal.cn: maybe not 与 maybe so 是最容易记的两对，一个关上一个打开可能性。

normal.en: A big maybe is the informal noun use, for something still undecided.
normal.cn: a big maybe 是它的非正式名词用法，指还悬着的事。

abstract.en: Picture two coins still swinging on a balance, never settling on one side.
abstract.cn: 想象天平上两枚硬币还在晃，始终不落向一边。

abstract.en: Saying maybe is like leaving a door half open so that either answer can walk in.
abstract.cn: 说 maybe 就像把门留半开，让哪个答案都能走进来。

abstract.en: Two short verbs joined into one word show how English compresses a whole hesitant sentence into a few sounds.
abstract.cn: 两个短动词并成一个词，正好显示英语如何把一整句犹豫的话压成很少的音节。

examples.en: Maybe the rain will stop before we reach the station.
examples.cn: 也许我们到站之前雨就会停。

examples.en: Maybe we should call her before we drive over.
examples.cn: 也许我们该在开车过去之前给她打个电话。

examples.en: The trip is still a maybe until the tickets are booked.
examples.cn: 在机票订好之前，这趟旅行还说不准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「妹比」——妹妹和别人比，谁更好还说不准；记住 maybe 是「也许」。

root: 由古英语 magan（能够）演变来的 may 与古英语 beon（是、存在）演变来的 be 合并而成；中古英语后期写成一词，作副词使用。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an open possibility; from it come the plain adverb, the polite suggestion, the hesitant answer, and the informal noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个开放的可能性；由此分出普通副词用法、客气建议、含糊回答，以及非正式的名词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance still swinging, with neither side yet resting on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平还在轻晃，两端都没有落到桌上。

branches.en: a forecast that keeps both options open
branches.cn: 一份把两种可能都留着的天气预报

branches.en: a hand raised before anyone starts driving
branches.cn: 还没发动车子前抬起的一只手

branches.en: a bare maybe given to a question
branches.cn: 对一个问题只回一句「或许吧」

branches.en: a plan sitting on the table without a date
branches.cn: 摊在桌上却没有日期的计划

branches.en: a word that turns doubt into something you can hold
branches.cn: 一个把犹豫变成可以拿在手里的东西的词

intro.en: The word is two Old English verbs welded together, and both pieces still show in the spelling.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个古英语动词焊在一起，两个部件在拼写里仍然看得见。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word, which is an English compound of two Old English verbs.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它是由两个古英语动词构成的英语复合词。

may 是 magan 磨短后的现在形式。
beon 是现代 be 的古英语来源。
be 是 maybe 的后半部分。
maybe 由两个词合并而成。
might 与 may 同出一源。
-an 标出 magan 的不定式身份。

items.meaningCN: be 的一个现在式形式
items.exampleCN: is 是 be 的一个现在式形式。

definition_zh: 钱；货币；财富；款项
definition_en: coins and notes used to buy things; wealth in general; funds collected or set aside for a purpose; the pay received for work
core_image: 铁盒里一叠皱巴巴的纸币，被手指一张张抹平
scene: 集市快收摊了，父亲把皱巴巴的纸币一张张抹平，再塞进旧铁盒。 He counted the money twice before putting it in the tin.
sceneCN: 这里 money 是「钱、货币」（第 1 个义项：用来买东西的钱币）；句意为他把钱数了两遍，才放进铁盒。画面里能想见：收摊的集市、皱巴巴的纸币、旧铁盒。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 monet- 加 -ary 构成，义为「货币的；金融的」
由 monet- 加 -ize 构成，义为「使货币化；靠……赚钱」
由 money 加 -ed 构成，义为「有钱的」
由 money 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无钱的」

senses.title: Coins and notes used to buy things
senses.definition: the coins and notes that people use to buy and sell things
senses.definitionCN: 人们用来买卖东西的硬币与纸币
senses.example: He counted the money twice before putting it in the tin.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钱数了两遍，才放进铁盒。
senses.why: The Latin word moneta began as the name of the mint where Roman coins were struck, then slid from the place of making to the thing made.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 moneta 起初是罗马铸币厂的名字，后来从「制造的地点」滑到「造出来的东西」。

senses.title: Wealth in general
senses.definition: wealth considered as a whole, including property and savings as well as cash
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体看待的财富，除现金外还包括房产与积蓄
senses.example: The family lost all its money in the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 这场火让这家人失去了全部财产。
senses.why: Once a word means coins, it easily widens to everything those coins can buy, so money comes to stand for the whole pile rather than the pieces.
senses.whyCN: 一个词一旦指硬币，就很容易扩到这些硬币能买下的一切；于是 money 转而指整堆财富，而不是一枚枚硬币。

senses.title: Funds set aside for a purpose
senses.definition: money collected or kept for a particular aim, such as building a school or running a service
senses.definitionCN: 为某个特定目标筹集或留存的钱，如建校或维持服务
senses.example: The council put public money into the new library.
senses.exampleCN: 议会把公共资金投进了新图书馆。
senses.why: Money is countable in this sense as sums set apart: the word no longer asks what you own but what has been assigned to a job.
senses.whyCN: 在这个义项里，money 可以按「分拨出来的款项」计数：它问的不再是你有多少，而是哪一笔钱被派了什么用途。

senses.title: Pay received for work
senses.definition: the amount a person is paid for their work, often judged as good or bad
senses.definitionCN: 一个人工作所得的报酬，常以高低来评价
senses.example: The money is good, but the hours are long.
senses.exampleCN: 报酬不错，可是工时太长。
senses.why: When money is what a job hands over, the same word measures a wage, and the phrase the money is good simply reports that the pay is generous.
senses.whyCN: 当 money 指一份工作交到你手里的东西时，同一个词就在衡量工资；the money is good 这句话只是说明报酬丰厚。

intro.en: Money comes from a Latin name for a mint, which itself grew from a verb meaning to warn; the place of coin-making gave its name to the coins.
intro.cn: money 来自拉丁语中对铸币厂的称呼，而那个称呼又长自动词「警告」；造币之地把自己的名字给了造出来的钱。

items.en: Monere meant to warn or to advise, and it stands behind the epithet of Juno whose temple held the Roman mint.
items.cn: monere 意为警告、提醒，朱诺的称号就由它而来，而罗马铸币厂正设在朱诺神庙里。

items.en: Moneta first named the mint, the place where silver was struck into coin, and later the coin itself.
items.cn: moneta 先指铸币厂，即把白银打成硬币的地方，后来也指硬币本身。

items.en: A monetarius was an officer of the mint, and the adjective monetarius described anything belonging to coining.
items.cn: monetarius 是铸币厂的官吏，而同形的形容词表示「与铸币有关的」。

items.en: Old French moneie carried the coin sense and also the sense of coined wealth into everyday use.
items.cn: 古法语 moneie 把「硬币」义以及「由钱构成的财富」义带入日常使用。

items.en: Modern English money keeps the mass-noun sense, adds funds and pay, and allows the formal plural monies for separate sums.
items.cn: 现代英语的 money 保留不可数名词的用法，又添上「资金」与「报酬」，并允许用正式复数 monies 指分开的多笔款项。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin mint word and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for cash, circulating value and wealth.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「铸币厂」一词及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示现金、流通价值与财富的词。

entries.definition: Connected with money or the currency of a country.
entries.definitionCN: 与货币或一国通货有关的。

entries.definition: To turn something into a source of money.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物变成赚钱的来源。

entries.definition: Rich, or coming from wealthy people.
entries.definitionCN: 有钱的，或来自富裕阶层的。

entries.definition: The place where a country makes its coins.
entries.definitionCN: 一国制造硬币的地方；铸币厂。

entries.definition: Coins and notes in hand, rather than money in an account.
entries.definitionCN: 手头的硬币和纸币，区别于账户里的钱。

entries.definition: The money a country uses and that is accepted in it.
entries.definitionCN: 一国使用并在该国通行的货币。

entries.definition: A large amount of money and property owned by someone.
entries.definitionCN: 某人拥有的大量钱财与财产。

entries.definition: Money available to be spent for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 可供用于某个目的的钱；资金。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the name of a building where coins were made, and its family keeps returning to mints, currency and the wealth coins stand for.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是一处造币建筑的名字，词族反复回到铸币厂、通货，以及硬币所代表的财富。

normal.en: Moneta is Latin for a mint, so money first names the place where coin is made, then the coin that came out.
normal.cn: moneta 是拉丁语的「铸币厂」，所以 money 先指造币的地方，再指造出来的硬币。

normal.en: Monetary adds -ary to the stem monet-: anything belonging to money.
normal.cn: monetary 在词干 monet- 后加 -ary：属于货币的一切。

normal.en: Monetize adds -ize: to turn a thing into money or into a way of earning.
normal.cn: monetize 加 -ize：把某样东西变成钱或变成赚钱的方式。

normal.en: Moneyed adds -ed: supplied with money, therefore rich.
normal.cn: moneyed 加 -ed：有钱供着，因而是富有的。

normal.en: Money is usually uncountable, so we say much money or a sum of money, not a money.
normal.cn: money 通常不可数，所以说 much money 或 a sum of money，而不说 a money。

abstract.en: A mint is a room where metal is pressed into promises; the word carries that promise long after the building is gone.
abstract.cn: 铸币厂是把金属压成承诺的房间；建筑早已不在，这个词仍带着那份承诺。

abstract.en: The same word covers a coin, a fortune and a budget because all three are the same thing at different scales.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖一枚硬币、一笔家产和一份预算，因为这三者只是同一件东西的不同尺度。

abstract.en: Counting money twice is an old habit: value felt in the hand is heavier than value written in an account.
abstract.cn: 把钱数两遍是老习惯：握在手里的价值，比写在账上的价值更沉。

examples.en: He counted the money twice before putting it in the tin.
examples.cn: 他把钱数了两遍，才放进铁盒。

examples.en: The family lost all its money in the fire.
examples.cn: 这场火让这家人失去了全部财产。

examples.en: The council put public money into the new library.
examples.cn: 议会把公共资金投进了新图书馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马尼」——听着像马驮着的尼龙袋，里面装的全是钱；money 就是钱。

root: 拉丁语 moneta（罗马的铸币厂，设在朱诺神庙）经古法语 moneie 进入英语；同族词多与铸币、货币、财富有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is coin struck at a mint; the senses widen from coin to the whole of one's wealth, to funds tied to a purpose, and to the pay a job brings.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是在铸币厂打出的硬币；义项从硬币扩到全部家产、指定用途的资金，以及工作带来的报酬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of crumpled notes being smoothed flat and tucked into a tin box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠皱巴巴的纸币被抹平，塞进铁盒。

branches.en: a handful of coins pushed across a counter
branches.cn: 几枚硬币被推过柜台

branches.en: a tin box holding the savings of a whole family
branches.cn: 一只装着一家人积蓄的铁盒

branches.en: a house and a field counted as one estate
branches.cn: 把房子和田地算作同一份家产

branches.en: a labelled jar of funds for a new roof
branches.cn: 贴着标签、攒着修屋顶的资金罐

branches.en: a pay slip read twice at the kitchen table
branches.cn: 在厨房桌上看了两遍的工资单

intro.en: A Latin verb of warning, the mint it named, the officer of that mint and four English endings carry the word from a building to cash, wealth and pay.
intro.cn: 一个表示「警告」的拉丁动词、它命名的铸币厂、厂里的官吏，以及四个英语词尾，把这个词从一座建筑带到了现金、财富与报酬。

latinIntro.en: Monere, moneta and monetarius are recorded Latin forms; the mint word is the direct ancestor of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: monere、moneta 与 monetarius 都是有记录的拉丁词形，其中表示铸币厂的那个词是英语名词的直接祖先。

definition_zh: 历史学家；史学研究者；编史者
definition_en: a person who studies and writes about the past, especially by examining evidence
core_image: 一张堆满手稿的长桌，学者戴着薄手套比对两封字迹不同的信
scene: 为了弄清末代码头的归属，一位研究者花了十年翻阅港口账簿与地图，被同行称为严谨的历史学家。 To settle who owned the old wharf, one researcher spent ten years reading port ledgers and maps, and colleagues called her a rigorous historian.
sceneCN: 这里 historian 指「以史料研究并书写过去的专业人员」（第 1 个义项：专业史学研究者）；句意为为了弄清末代码头归属，一位研究者花十年翻阅港口账簿与地图，被同行称为严谨的历史学家。可辨识物件：手稿长桌、薄手套、两封信、港口地图。

pos.zh: 历史学家；史学研究者（可数）

derivatives.zh: 历史；历史学
历史的；史学的
有历史意义的
编史学；史学史
编史者；官方史官

senses.title: A professional student of the past
senses.definition: a scholar trained to find, check and interpret evidence about past events
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、能查找、核验并解释过去事件证据的学者
senses.example: The historian spent a decade in the port ledgers before writing a single chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史学家在港口账簿里花了十年，才写下一章。
senses.why: the -ian ending marks a practitioner, so historian is the person behind the discipline of history.
senses.whyCN: -ian 词尾标记从业者，因此 historian 就是历史学科背后的人。

senses.title: A writer of narrative history
senses.definition: an author who turns evidence into a readable account for a general audience
senses.definitionCN: 把证据变成公众可读叙述的作者
senses.example: As a historian she writes for readers who have never opened an archive.
senses.exampleCN: 作为历史写作者，她为从未进过档案馆的读者写作。
senses.why: history once meant story, so the person who shapes the narrative keeps the older role.
senses.whyCN: history 曾经意为故事，因此把材料塑造成叙述的人延续了更古老的角色。

senses.title: An archival researcher
senses.definition: a specialist who works mainly on documents, registers and provenance rather than on broad narrative
senses.definitionCN: 主要处理文书、登记册与来源考证，而非宏大叙述的专家
senses.example: The provenance of the painting was settled by a historian of tax records.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画的来历由一位研究税收档案的历史学家厘清。
senses.why: the discipline's authority rests on evidence, so one identity of the historian is the person who follows paper trails.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科权威来自证据，因此历史学家的一重身份就是顺着纸面线索追查的人。

senses.title: An official or court chronicler
senses.definition: a person appointed to record events for a ruler, a city or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 受命为统治者、城市或机构记录事件的人
senses.example: The court historian recorded the campaign in a tone the general approved.
senses.exampleCN: 宫廷史官以一种将军认可的语调记录了这场战役。
senses.why: the office predates the modern profession, and appointment shaped what could be written.
senses.whyCN: 这一职位早于现代专业，任命本身决定了什么可以写。

senses.title: A historian of one field
senses.definition: a specialist in the past of a particular subject, such as science, art or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定主题（如科学、艺术或医学）之过去的专家
senses.example: A historian of medicine traced the shift from bleeding to transfusion.
senses.exampleCN: 一位医学史学家梳理了从放血到输血的转变。
senses.why: as disciplines multiplied, each needed its own reader of its records, so the word took a field complement.
senses.whyCN: 学科不断增多，每一门都需要自己的档案解读者，于是这个词带上了领域补语。

senses.title: An institutional historian
senses.definition: a person who writes the history of a company, a school or a regiment, often from internal files
senses.definitionCN: 依据内部档案撰写公司、学校或团队历史的人
senses.example: The firm's historian was given the whole correspondence of its founders.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的史学家获准查阅创始人的全部通信。
senses.why: institutions need a usable past, so they hire someone to turn their files into a lineage.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个可用的过去，于是雇人把档案变成一条传承线。

senses.title: An amateur or local historian
senses.definition: a non-professional who documents the past of a place or a family with care but without formal training
senses.definitionCN: 非专业者，认真记录某地或某家族过去，但未受正式训练
senses.example: A local historian mapped every well that had disappeared from the village.
senses.exampleCN: 一位地方史研究者标出了村里每一口消失的水井。
senses.why: the role is defined by the subject and the care, not by a degree, so the word admits amateurs.
senses.whyCN: 这一角色由主题与用心程度界定，而非由学位界定，因此也容纳业余者。

senses.title: Abstract: anyone who explains the past
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何解释过去的人
senses.definition: loosely, anyone who offers an account of how something came to be
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛地指任何讲述某事物如何形成的人
senses.example: Every family has its own historian, usually the one who keeps the photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 每个家庭都有自己的史学家，通常是保存照片的那位。
senses.why: the abstract use keeps only the act of accounting for the past, dropping the archive and the degree.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法只保留「为过去作说明」这一动作，去掉档案与学位。

intro.en: Historian is history plus the person-ending -ian, modelled on French historien. The root goes back to Greek histor 'witness, one who knows'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: historian 是 history 加表示人的词尾 -ian，仿法语 historien 构成。词根可追溯到希腊 histor「见证人、知情者」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Histor meant 'witness, one who knows', generally linked to the root for seeing that also underlies English wit.
items.cn: histor 意为「见证人、知情者」，一般与表示「看见」的词根相联系，英语 wit 亦出此根。

items.en: Historia was inquiry and the knowledge gained by it, the title word of early prose research.
items.cn: historia 是探究及由此获得的知识，是早期散文研究的标题词。

items.en: Latin kept historia for both the inquiry and the written account, and the account sense became dominant.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留 historia 兼指探究与成文记述，后来记述义占主导。

items.en: French formed historien for the person, adding the agent ending to the noun; English borrowed the pattern in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语在名词上加施事词尾，构成指人的 historien；英语于 16 世纪借用这一构词模式。

items.en: Historian first meant a writer of histories, and only later a salaried academic researcher with methods and archives.
items.cn: historian 最初指写史之人，后来才指领取薪俸、有方法与档案的学院研究者。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation of historian is not firmly fixed, and the pre-Greek history of histor is unsettled, so any reconstructed root is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：historian 在英语中的最早书证并不确定；histor 在希腊语之前的历史亦未定，任何重构词根都是假说。

note.en: Group one holds the adjective and root forms most often confused with the person; group two holds neighbouring keepers of the past.
note.cn: 第一组是常与「人」混淆的形容词与同根形式；第二组是相邻的「过去守护者」。

entries.definition: Describes an event important enough to be remembered; it is not the person who studies events.
entries.definitionCN: 形容重要到值得被记住的事件；不是研究事件的人。

entries.definition: Describes anything connected with the past or with the discipline; the person form is historian.
entries.definitionCN: 形容与过去或该学科有关的任何事物；指人的形式是 historian。

entries.definition: The record, discipline or account itself; historian is the practitioner of that field.
entries.definitionCN: 指记录、学科或叙述本身；historian 是该领域的从业者。

entries.definition: The analysis of how histories are written; a historian may practise historiography, but the words are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 对历史如何被书写的分析；历史学家可以从事编史学研究，但两词不可互换。

entries.definition: One who writes a chronicle, an event-by-event record; the role is closer to listing than to interpreting.
entries.definitionCN: 写编年史的人，逐事记录；其角色更接近罗列而非解释。

entries.definition: A formal title for an appointed writer of history, especially of a state or institution.
entries.definitionCN: 受任撰写历史者的正式头衔，尤指国家或机构的史官。

entries.definition: A person who preserves and catalogues documents; the archivist keeps the evidence a historian reads.
entries.definitionCN: 保存并编目文书的人；档案员保管历史学家所读的证据。

entries.definition: An older word for one who studies ancient objects and records, often as a collector rather than an analyst.
entries.definitionCN: 旧称，指研究古物与古记录的人，常是收藏者而非分析者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real set phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: history plus -ian makes the person, as music makes musician and politics makes politician.
normal.cn: history 加 -ian 构成指人的词，正如 music 构成 musician、politics 构成 politician。

normal.en: The root histor means witness, the one who was there and can tell.
normal.cn: 词根 histor 意为见证人，即在场并能讲述的人。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the specialisms: military historian, art historian, historian of science.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出专长：军事史学家、艺术史学家、科学史学家。

normal.en: The adjective historic means momentous; historical means relating to the past.
normal.cn: 形容词 historic 指重大，historical 指与过去有关。

normal.en: An archivist keeps the papers; a historian reads them and argues.
normal.cn: 档案员保管纸页，历史学家阅读并论证。

abstract.en: Picture thin gloves lifting two letters written in different hands.
abstract.cn: 想象薄手套捧起两封字迹不同的信。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger trail that leads from a tax entry to a whole family.
abstract.cn: 想象一条账簿线索，从一条税目通向一整个家族。

abstract.en: Picture a family album kept by the one person who remembers every name.
abstract.cn: 想象一本家庭相册，由一个记得所有名字的人保管。

examples.en: Historians disagree about the cause of the fire, though they share the same files.
examples.cn: 历史学家对这场火灾的成因意见不一，尽管他们看的是同一批档案。

examples.en: A military historian reconstructed the march from supply receipts.
examples.cn: 一位军事史学家依据补给收据重建了这次行军。

examples.en: The local historian found the well under a car park.
examples.cn: 地方史研究者在停车场下找到了那口井。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「history（历史）+ an（人）」——写历史的那个人 → 历史学家

root: history + -ian（表人词尾），仿法语 historien；词根回溯希腊 histor「见证人、知情者」，一般与 idein「看见」同根。histor 的更深来源不确定。英语 historian。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one person from the professional scholar to the narrative writer, the archive specialist, the official chronicler, the field specialist, the institutional and amateur worker, and finally anyone who explains a past.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种人展开：专业学者、叙事作者、档案考证者、官方史官、领域专家、机构史撰写者与业余研究者，最后是任何解释过去的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table of manuscripts and a pair of gloved hands comparing two letters.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张手稿长桌，戴手套的双手比对两封信。

branches.en: TRAINED READER: the professional identity rests on handling evidence correctly.
branches.cn: 受过训练的读者：专业身份建立在正确处置证据之上。

branches.en: STORYTELLER: the narrative role keeps the oldest sense of history as story.
branches.cn: 讲故事的人：叙事角色保留了 history 作为故事的最早义项。

branches.en: APPOINTED VOICE: rulers and institutions need a past written in their own files.
branches.cn: 受命发声：统治者与机构需要一段依自家档案写成的过去。

branches.en: FIELD SPECIALIST: every discipline trains its own reader of its records.
branches.cn: 领域专家：每门学科都训练自己的档案解读者。

branches.en: CARE WITHOUT A DEGREE: the role finally opens to anyone who keeps and explains the past.
branches.cn: 无关学位的用心：这一角色最终向任何守护并解释过去的人开放。

intro.en: Historian is a transparent construction: a Greek-derived noun plus the Latin-derived person ending -ian, the same ending as in musician.
intro.cn: historian 的结构很透明：希腊来源名词加拉丁来源的表人词尾 -ian，与 musician 中的词尾相同。

latinIntro.en: Latin historia builds history and historiography; the ending -ianus, through French -ien, gives the English person suffix -ian.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 historia 构成 history 与 historiography；拉丁词尾 -ianus 经法语 -ien 给出英语表人词尾 -ian。

items.example: historian is the person of history.
items.exampleCN: historian 就是从事历史的人。

items.example: The historian read the port ledgers.
items.exampleCN: 这位历史学家读了港口账簿。
那项裁决具有历史意义。

items.example: Historiography examines how accounts are built.
items.exampleCN: 编史学研究叙述如何被建构。

definition_zh: 做；制造；使得；作出；赚得；品牌
definition_en: to produce or create something, to cause something to happen or be, to carry out an action, to earn money, or, as a noun, the brand of a product
core_image: 一双手把散落的材料按在一起，桌上慢慢出现一个成形的东西
scene: 厨房里灯还亮着，面粉撒在案板上，孩子踮着脚看大人揉面。 She made the dough before sunrise and left it covered by the window.
sceneCN: 这里是「做、制作」（第 1 个义项：把材料做成东西）；句意为她在日出前和好面团，盖上布放在窗边。

derivatives.zh: 由 make 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「制作者；制造商」
由 make 加 -ing 构成名词，义为「制作；形成过程」
由前缀 re-（再次）加 make 构成，义为「重做；翻拍」

senses.title: To produce or create something
senses.definition: to produce, build or create something out of materials or parts
senses.definitionCN: 用材料或零件做出、建造或创造某物
senses.example: She made a small wooden box for her letters.
senses.exampleCN: 她给信件做了一个小木盒。
senses.why: Old English macian meant to build or fashion, so the first sense is a hand shaping raw material into an object.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 macian 意为建造、塑形，所以第一个义项是手把原料塑成物件。

senses.title: To cause someone or something to be or do something
senses.definition: to cause a person or thing to enter a state or to perform an action
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物进入某种状态，或去做某事
senses.example: The news made everyone quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让所有人都安静下来。
senses.why: Once a hand can shape clay, the same verb is stretched to shaping events: what you do makes a result happen.
senses.whyCN: 既然手能塑造黏土，同一个动词就被延伸到塑造事件：你所做的使某个结果发生。

senses.title: To perform an action
senses.definition: to perform an action, especially one that is named by a noun, such as make a decision or make an effort
senses.definitionCN: 执行某个动作，尤其是由名词命名的动作，如作出决定、付出努力
senses.example: They made a careful decision before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 签字之前他们作了慎重的决定。
senses.why: English often pairs a light verb with an action noun, and make is the light verb that turns the noun into something actually done.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把轻动词与动作名词搭配，make 正是那个把名词变成真正做出来的事的轻动词。

senses.title: To earn or gain money
senses.definition: to earn money or gain a profit from work, trade or an investment
senses.definitionCN: 通过工作、买卖或投资挣到钱或获得利润
senses.example: The stall made a small profit on its first day.
senses.exampleCN: 这个摊子在开张头一天赚了一点钱。
senses.why: Producing goods that sell turns the verb for making objects into the verb for making money.
senses.whyCN: 把做出来的东西卖出去，就使「制造物件」的动词变成「赚到钱」的动词。

senses.title: The brand of a manufactured product
senses.definition: the brand or particular type under which a product is manufactured and sold
senses.definitionCN: 产品被制造和销售时所标的品牌或特定型号
senses.example: The two cars are the same model but a different make.
senses.exampleCN: 这两辆车是同一款，但品牌不同。
senses.why: A workshop name marked what it turned out, and that mark became the noun for the brand itself.
senses.whyCN: 作坊的名字标示它做出来的东西，这个标记后来就成了指品牌本身的名词。

intro.en: Make is a West Germanic verb for building that widened into causing, performing, earning and the name of a brand.
intro.cn: make 是西日耳曼语中表示建造的动词，后来词义扩展到致使、执行、赚钱以及品牌的名称。

items.en: macian meant to make, build or form, and it was one of the commonest verbs in the language.
items.cn: macian 意为制作、建造、塑形，是当时最常用的动词之一。

items.en: The reconstructed form *makōjanan meant to fashion or put together and is generally taken to be shared with other Germanic verbs of the same meaning.
items.cn: 重构形式 *makōjanan 意为塑形、拼合，一般认为它与其他日耳曼语中同义的动词同出一源。

items.en: macian became maken, and the meaning widened from building to any kind of doing.
items.cn: macian 演变为 maken，词义从建造扩大到各种「做」。

items.en: The pattern make someone do something became ordinary, and so did make in the sense of earning a living.
items.cn: 「让某人做某事」的句式和「谋生、挣钱」的用法在这时都变得平常。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb in hundreds of phrases and adds the noun make for the brand of a product.
items.cn: 现代英语让这个动词留在大量短语里，并添上名词用法，指产品的品牌。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built directly on make; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for bringing something into existence.
note.cn: 形近组收直接建立在 make 上的形式；近义组收表示使某物产生的动词。

entries.definition: A person or company that makes something.
entries.definitionCN: 制造某物的人或公司。

entries.definition: The act or process of producing something.
entries.definitionCN: 生产某物的动作或过程。

entries.definition: To make something again, or a new version of an old work.
entries.definitionCN: 重做某物，或旧作品的新版本。

entries.definition: Cosmetics, or the way parts are put together.
entries.definitionCN: 化妆品，或各部分的组成方式。

entries.definition: To bring something new into existence.
entries.definitionCN: 使新事物产生。

entries.definition: To make goods in large amounts, especially for sale.
entries.definitionCN: 大量制造商品，尤指供出售。

entries.definition: To make goods in a factory using machines.
entries.definitionCN: 在工厂里用机器制造商品。

entries.definition: To put parts together to form a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 把各部分组合成结构。

normalIntro.en: The word is a common Germanic verb for shaping material, and its uses spread from the workshop to causes, actions, wages and brands.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中表示塑造材料的常用动词，用法从作坊扩散到原因、行动、收入和品牌。

normal.en: Make is the everyday verb for turning material into an object, just as macian was in Old English.
normal.cn: make 是把材料变成物件的日常动词，古英语里的 macian 也是如此。

normal.en: Maker adds -er to make, so the person who makes is simply the verb plus a doer ending.
normal.cn: maker 在 make 后加 -er，所以「制作者」不过是动词加上表示做事者的词尾。

normal.en: The pattern make him wait is a shortcut: instead of doing the action, you cause someone else to do it.
normal.cn: 「让他等」这种句式是一种捷径：你不亲自做，而是使别人去做。

normal.en: Make a decision sounds strange in some languages, but English uses make as a light verb for actions named by nouns.
normal.cn: 「作出决定」在某些语言里说法不同，但英语把 make 当作轻动词，与名词命名的动作搭配。

normal.en: The noun make for a car brand comes from the workshop mark, not from the act of building.
normal.cn: 指汽车品牌的名词 make 来自作坊的标记，而不是来自建造这个动作。

abstract.en: Flour, water and a pair of hands: the table is empty, and then there is dough.
abstract.cn: 面粉、水和一双手：案板先是空的，然后就有了面团。

abstract.en: One sentence can push another person across a room without touching them, and English calls that making.
abstract.cn: 一句话不碰到任何人，就能把别人推得满屋走动，英语把这种作用叫作 make。

abstract.en: A name stamped on a car door outlives the hands that built it, and that name is the make.
abstract.cn: 印在车门上的名字比造它的那双手活得更久，那个名字就是 make。

examples.en: She made a small wooden box for her letters.
examples.cn: 她给信件做了一个小木盒。

examples.en: The news made everyone quiet.
examples.cn: 这个消息让所有人都安静下来。

examples.en: The two cars are the same model but a different make.
examples.cn: 这两辆车是同一款，但品牌不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克」——麦克风递到谁手里，谁就得当场做点什么；记住 make 是做。

root: 古英语 macian（制作、建造）源自西日耳曼语，一般认为与重构形式 *makōjanan 同源；同族词多与「做、制成、制作者」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the hand shaping material into an object; the word then extends to causing results, performing actions, earning money, and naming a brand.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是手把材料塑成物件；词义随后扩展到使结果发生、执行动作、挣得收入，以及给品牌命名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pressing loose material together until a shaped object appears on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手把松散的材料按在一起，桌上渐渐出现一个成形的物件。

branches.en: flour and water turning into dough under a pair of hands
branches.cn: 面粉与水在一双手下变成面团

branches.en: a single sentence that pushes someone into action
branches.cn: 一句话把别人推入行动

branches.en: a decision written down before the meeting begins
branches.cn: 会前就写好的决定

branches.en: coins counted at the end of a market day
branches.cn: 集市散场后数起的硬币

branches.en: two cars of the same make parked side by side
branches.cn: 两辆同品牌的车并排停着

intro.en: The word rests on one Old English verb, its irregular past form, and a set of suffixes and compounds that keep the idea of producing.
intro.cn: 这个词依靠一个古英语动词、它不规则的变化形式，以及一组保留「制作」含义的后缀与复合词支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; its recorded relatives are Germanic, including the reconstructed *makōjanan.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它的有据亲属属于日耳曼语，包括重构形式 *makōjanan。

items.meaning: to make again; a new version

definition_zh: 拥抱；搂抱；（名词）拥抱
definition_en: to put your arms around someone and hold them close to show love or comfort
core_image: 两条手臂围成的一个圈：把一个人整个圈进怀里
scene: 火车进站，妹妹冲过人群扑进哥哥怀里。 She gave her brother a big hug at the station.
sceneCN: 这里 hug 是名词「拥抱」（第 1 个义项：搂抱的动作）；她在车站给了哥哥一个大大的拥抱。

senses.title: To hold someone close with the arms
senses.definition: to put your arms around someone and press them close
senses.definitionCN: 用双臂环住某人并紧紧搂在怀里
senses.example: Grandma hugged the children before they left for school.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们上学前，奶奶把他们搂在怀里。
senses.why: The core act is two arms closing into a circle around a person.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是两条手臂围人合拢成一个圈。

senses.title: To hold or fit closely around something
senses.definition: to fit or stay very close to something, as clothes or a road hugging a shape
senses.definitionCN: 指衣服贴身，或道路紧贴地形延伸
senses.example: The road hugs the coast for twenty kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 公路沿着海岸线延伸了二十公里。
senses.why: Arms around a person become a border around a shape: the close circle moves onto things.
senses.whyCN: 环抱人的双臂变成围住轮廓的边线：这个「圈」挪到了事物上。

senses.title: To keep a feeling close to oneself
senses.definition: to keep a feeling secretly close inside oneself
senses.definitionCN: 把某种情感悄悄揣在心里
senses.example: She hugged the memory of that summer for many years.
senses.exampleCN: 那个夏天的记忆她珍藏了许多年。
senses.why: What the arms do to a person, the heart does to a memory: held close and not let go.
senses.whyCN: 手臂对人所做的，心对记忆也照做：紧紧收着，不肯松开。

intro.en: Hug is a Nordic word borrowed into English in the sixteenth century; Old Norse hugga meant to comfort.
intro.cn: hug 是十六世纪从北欧借入英语的词；古诺斯语 hugga 意为安慰。

items.en: Old Norse hugga meant to comfort and soothe, built on hugr, meaning mind and spirit.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 hugga 意为安抚、慰藉，词根是 hugr「心灵、精神」。

items.en: Danish and Norwegian kept related words for comforting embraces.
items.cn: 丹麦语、挪威语保留了表示安慰式拥抱的关联词。

items.en: There are rare Middle English traces, but the word settled later.
items.cn: 中古英语偶见踪迹，但真正定型较晚。

items.en: From the sixteenth century, hug named the close embrace itself.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，hug 指那种紧紧的拥抱。

items.en: Modern English widened it to roads, clothes and hidden feelings.
items.cn: 现代英语又把它扩展到道路、衣物与藏于心底的情感。

note.en: Group one keeps the embrace family; group two keeps close-contact near words.
note.cn: 第一组是拥抱词族；第二组是亲密接触的近义词。

entries.definition: the past form of hug, with double g
entries.definitionCN: hug 的过去式，双写 g 再加 ed

entries.definition: so soft that people want to hug it
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「让人想抱的」

entries.definition: the centre of a wheel or network; only spelling is close
entries.definitionCN: hub 是「轮毂；中心」，与 hug 只是拼写相近

entries.definition: to hold someone closely in the arms
entries.definitionCN: 拥抱，较正式的说法

entries.definition: to hold gently and lovingly for a long time
entries.definitionCN: 依偎；轻抚，时间长且温柔

entries.definition: to hold tightly with the hand or arms
entries.definitionCN: 紧握；紧抱，强调用力

normalIntro.en: Use the double-g spelling and the circle image.
normalIntro.cn: 用双写 g 的拼写与「圈」的意象记 hug。

normal.en: hug, hugged, hugging: double the g before -ed and -ing
normal.cn: hug 变形要双写 g：hugged、hugging。

normal.en: give somebody a hug is the everyday phrase
normal.cn: give somebody a hug 是日常说法：给个拥抱。

normal.en: a bear hug wraps you twice over
normal.cn: bear hug 熊抱＝把你整个裹住的大拥抱。

normal.en: Old Norse hugr means mind: the hug holds the heart
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 hugr 意为心：拥抱搂住的不只是身体。

normal.en: the road hugs the coast like an arm around a shoulder
normal.cn: 公路 hug 海岸，像手臂环着肩膀。

abstract.en: Picture two arms closing like a gate around one person.
abstract.cn: 想象两条手臂像两扇门在一个人身前合拢。

abstract.en: Picture a coat that hugs your shoulders on a cold morning.
abstract.cn: 想象冷天早晨紧贴肩头的外套——贴合义。

abstract.en: Feel a memory kept warm in the middle of the chest.
abstract.cn: 感受胸口正中被焐得温热的记忆——心怀义。

examples.en: The two friends hugged each other goodbye at the gate.
examples.cn: 两个朋友在大门口拥抱道别。

examples.en: A warm hug can say more than a long speech.
examples.cn: 一个温暖的拥抱胜过千言万语。

examples.en: The path hugs the river all the way to the village.
examples.cn: 小路沿着河流一直延伸到村庄。

sensesIntro.cn: hug 从环抱人的手臂，扩展到贴着海岸的公路、揣在心里的记忆。

definition_zh: 许多的；许多（人或物）；许多（后接单数名词）；多数人；大众
definition_en: a large number of countable things; used as a pronoun for a large group; in the pattern many a with a singular noun; and the many as the ordinary majority
core_image: 广场上站满了人，一眼望去数不清有多少张脸
scene: 雨刚停，剧场门口的人已经排成长队，伞还在滴水。 By the time the doors opened, many people had already been waiting for hours.
sceneCN: 这里指数目很多的人（第 1 个义项：许多的）；句意为开门时已经有许多人等了几个小时。

derivatives.zh: 由 many 与后缀 -fold（倍）复合，义为「许多倍的；成倍地」
由 many 与 sided 复合，义为「多方面的；多边的」
由 many-sided 加 -ness 构成，义为「多面性」

senses.title: A large number of countable things
senses.definition: used before a plural countable noun to say that the number of things or people is large
senses.definitionCN: 用在可数名词复数前，表示人或物的数目很大
senses.example: Many students walk to the library after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 许多学生午饭后步行去图书馆。
senses.why: Old English manig was already an adjective of quantity used with plurals, so the first job of the word is simply to put a large count in front of a noun.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 manig 本来就是与复数连用的数量形容词，所以这个词最初的工作，就是把一个很大的数目放在名词前面。

senses.title: A large number already mentioned
senses.definition: used as a pronoun, usually with of, for a large number of people or things that the listener can identify
senses.definitionCN: 作代词使用，常与 of 连用，指听者能够识别的一大群人或物
senses.example: Many of the old houses were built by the same family.
senses.exampleCN: 这些老房子有许多是同一家人建的。
senses.why: When the noun is dropped, the quantity word has to stand on its own, and of supplies the group it counts; the hearer fills in the rest from context.
senses.whyCN: 名词被省掉后，这个数量词只能自己站住，而 of 引出它所清点的群体；其余部分由听者根据上下文补足。

senses.title: Many a followed by a singular noun
senses.definition: a formal or literary pattern in which many a is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb, though the meaning is a large number
senses.definitionCN: 正式或文学性的结构：many a 后接单数名词与单数动词，但表达的是「许多」
senses.example: Many a sailor has told the same story about that storm.
senses.exampleCN: 许多水手都讲过关于那场风暴的同一个故事。
senses.why: The pattern counts one member at a time, which is why the noun and verb stay singular, yet the repetition adds up to a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这个结构一次只点一个成员，所以名词和动词都用单数；但一次次相加，最后仍是一个群体。

senses.title: The many as the ordinary majority
senses.definition: the large group of ordinary people, especially when set against a small group with power or wealth
senses.definitionCN: 普通人的大多数，尤指与掌握权力或财富的少数群体相对时
senses.example: The policy was praised by the few and ignored by the many.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策得到少数人称赞，却被多数人忽视。
senses.why: With the definite article, many stops being a count and becomes a name for a social body, the crowd that stands opposite the few.
senses.whyCN: 带上定冠词之后，many 不再清点数量，而成为对一个社会群体的称呼：与少数人相对的众人。

intro.en: Many is a Germanic quantity adjective that has stayed close to its Old English form and keeps company with German manch and Dutch menig.
intro.cn: many 是日耳曼语的数量形容词，形态与古英语时期相距不远，并与德语 manch、荷兰语 menig 同属一族。

items.en: The word appears as manig or monig, an adjective of quantity meaning many or much, used with plural nouns.
items.cn: 这个词写作 manig 或 monig，是表示数量的形容词，意为许多、大量，与复数名词连用。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective *managaz is the common source of the English, German and Dutch forms.
items.cn: 重构形容词 *managaz 是英语、德语与荷兰语诸形式的共同来源。

items.en: Old Norse margr and German manch are cousins, which shows the word was a shared Germanic way of counting a crowd.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 margr 与德语 manch 是近亲，说明这个词是日耳曼语各支共有的清点人群的说法。

items.en: Middle English kept many for plural count nouns and paired it with much for masses, fixing the countable and uncountable split.
items.cn: 中古英语让 many 专管可数名词复数，与管不可数量的 much 配对，固定了可数与不可数的分工。

items.en: Modern English adds the pronoun use with of, the formal pattern many a, and the noun phrase the many for the ordinary majority.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了与 of 连用的代词用法、正式的 many a 结构，以及指普通大众的名词短语 the many。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers quantity words built on or paired with the same Germanic root; the near-meaning group gathers words for a large number.
note.cn: 形近组收同一日耳曼词根上的数量词或与之配对的词；近义组收表示数量众多的词。

entries.definition: The counterpart of many used with uncountable nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 与 many 相对、用于不可数名词的数量词。

entries.definition: The shared comparative of many and much, meaning a larger number or amount.
entries.definitionCN: many 与 much 共同的比较级，表示更多。

entries.definition: The shared superlative of many and much, meaning the largest number or amount.
entries.definitionCN: many 与 much 共同的最高级，表示最多。

entries.definition: Existing in many forms or copies; also a pipe with several branches.
entries.definitionCN: 有多种形式或许多份的；也指多支管的管道。

entries.definition: Existing in large numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 数量众多的，较正式。

entries.definition: Too many to be counted.
entries.definitionCN: 多得数不清的。

entries.definition: More than two but not a large number.
entries.definitionCN: 多于两个但不算很多。

entries.definition: A large amount, enough or more than enough.
entries.definitionCN: 大量；充足。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective of quantity whose form changed little, and whose grammar splits countable things from masses and from fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是形态变化很小的日耳曼语数量形容词，它的语法把可数事物、不可数总量和固定短语区分开来。

normal.en: Old English manig is the direct ancestor of many, and its -ig ending is the old adjective suffix for having a quality.
normal.cn: 古英语 manig 是 many 的直接祖先，其中的 -ig 词尾就是表示「具有某种性质」的古老形容词后缀。

normal.en: German manch and Dutch menig are cousins of many, which shows the word has been a Germanic quantity term all along.
normal.cn: 德语 manch 与荷兰语 menig 是 many 的近亲，说明这个词一直是日耳曼语的数量词。

normal.en: Many counts separate items and much measures a mass, so the two words divide the countable from the uncountable.
normal.cn: many 清点一件件分开的东西，much 衡量一团总量，两个词由此把可数与不可数分开。

normal.en: More and most are shared with much, which is why many never takes -er or -est.
normal.cn: more 与 most 是和 much 共用的，所以 many 从不加 -er 或 -est。

normal.en: Many a is followed by a singular noun and verb, while many alone takes a plural; the grammar marks the fixed pattern off from ordinary counting.
normal.cn: many a 后接单数名词与单数动词，而单独的 many 接复数；语法把这个固定结构与普通清点区分开来。

abstract.en: A crowd too dense to count is the simplest picture of many: the word begins with the failure of one-by-one counting.
abstract.cn: 一片多到数不清的人群，就是 many 最简单的画面：这个词从「没法一个个数」开始。

abstract.en: Saying many rather than much is a decision about how the world is sliced, into separate things or into a mass.
abstract.cn: 说 many 而不是 much，是在决定世界怎样被切开：切成一件件东西，还是看成一团总量。

abstract.en: The many and the few turn a number word into a picture of society, where counting becomes a question of who holds power.
abstract.cn: the many 与 the few 把一个数词变成社会图景，清点由此变成「谁掌握权力」的问题。

examples.en: Many students walk to the library after lunch.
examples.cn: 许多学生午饭后步行去图书馆。

examples.en: Many of the old houses were built by the same family.
examples.cn: 这些老房子有许多是同一家人建的。

examples.en: Many a sailor has told the same story about that storm.
examples.cn: 许多水手都讲过关于那场风暴的同一个故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「曼妮」——曼妮走到哪儿都有许多人围着；记住 many 是许多。

root: 古英语 manig（许多）一般认为源自原始日耳曼语重构形容词 *managaz；同族词有德语 manch 与荷兰语 menig，无可靠拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a large count of separate things; leaving out the noun makes a pronoun, a fixed singular pattern narrows the grammar, and the definite form turns the crowd into a social body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是对一件件可数事物的清点；省略名词后成为代词，固定的单数结构收窄了语法，而定冠形式则把这群人称社会群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square filled with people, too many to count one by one.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场上站满了人，多到无法一个个数清。

branches.cn: 大多数课桌都坐了人的教室

branches.cn: 一个数量先成为代词，再成为公众群体

intro.en: The word is held together by an Old English adjective, its adjective suffix, a reconstructed Germanic base, and the comparative and superlative forms it shares with much.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语形容词、它的形容词后缀、重构的日耳曼语词基，以及它与 much 共用的比较级和最高级共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for many; its relatives are Germanic, such as German manch and Dutch menig.
latinIntro.cn: many 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它的近亲属于日耳曼语，例如德语 manch 与荷兰语 menig。

definition_zh: 节日；节期；庆典；会演；（音乐、电影等的）节
definition_en: a special day or period of celebration, or an organized series of performances or events
core_image: 街道挂满彩灯与旗帜，人们从四面八方涌向同一片欢腾
scene: 元宵夜，孩子们提着灯笼挤在挂满灯谜的长街上。 The lantern festival draws crowds from every part of the city.
sceneCN: 这里 festival 是名词，指「节庆活动」，对应第 1 个义项；句意为灯会吸引了全城各处的人潮。

derivatives.zh: 节日的；欢庆的（festival 的词根加形容词后缀 -ive，指充满节日气氛）
庆典；欢庆活动（festive 加名词后缀 -ity，指欢乐的庆祝）
庆祝活动（festivity 的复数，指一系列庆祝）

senses.title: A special day of celebration
senses.definition: a special day or period when people celebrate something
senses.definitionCN: 人们举行庆祝的特殊日子或时段
senses.example: The Spring Festival is the biggest holiday in China.
senses.exampleCN: 春节是中国最大的节日。
senses.why: A fixed date turns ordinary time into a marked moment, so the word names the day itself.
senses.whyCN: 固定的日期把平常时光变成被标记的时刻，所以词首先指那个日子。

senses.title: An organized series of events
senses.definition: an organized set of performances, films or competitions held over several days
senses.definitionCN: 连日举行的表演、电影或比赛的系列安排
senses.example: The town hosts a jazz festival every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇每年夏天举办爵士音乐节。
senses.why: When the celebration becomes a programme, the day grows into an event series.
senses.whyCN: 当庆祝变成节目单，单日就扩展成系列活动。

senses.title: The joyful atmosphere of celebration
senses.definition: the lively mood and activities of a celebration
senses.definitionCN: 庆祝时的热闹气氛与活动
senses.example: The whole street was in festival mood.
senses.exampleCN: 整条街都沉浸在节日的欢乐中。
senses.why: The day is felt as much as marked: the word covers the mood it creates.
senses.whyCN: 节日既被标记也被感受：这个词也涵盖它制造的气氛。

intro.en: Festival descends from Latin festus 'of a feast, joyful', the same root that gives feast, and it arrived through Old French as both day and celebration.
intro.cn: festival 源自拉丁语 festus「宴会的、欢乐的」，与 feast 同根，经古法语传入，兼指日子与庆典。

items.en: Festus meant 'of a feast, joyous', marking days set aside for worship and meals.
items.cn: festus 意为「宴会的、欢乐的」，标记专用于祭拜与宴饮的日子。

items.en: Medieval Latin festum meant 'a feast day', the direct source of both feast and festival.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 festum 意为「节日」，是 feast 与 festival 的直接来源。

items.en: Old French feste kept the religious feast day sense.
items.cn: 古法语 feste 保留了宗教节日义。

items.en: Middle English borrowed feste as feast, and festival came later through the adjective line.
items.cn: 中古英语把 feste 借为 feast，festival 则经由形容词路线较晚到来。

items.en: Modern English uses festival for holidays and for organized event series like film festivals.
items.cn: 现代英语用 festival 指节日及电影节之类的系列活动。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fest root; near-meaning words cover holidays and public celebrations.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fest 词根；近义组覆盖假日与公共庆典。

entries.definition: a large special meal; from the same Latin line

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the fest root and common festival types.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自 fest 词根与常见节庆类型的记忆抓手。

normal.en: festival and feast share the root fest: a festival is a feast of days.
normal.cn: festival 与 feast 同含词根 fest：节日就是日子的盛宴。

normal.en: music festival, film festival: any art can fill the calendar.
normal.cn: music festival、film festival：任何艺术都能填满节庆日历。

normal.en: festive is the adjective: festive lights make a festival street.
normal.cn: festive 是形容词：节日的彩灯造就节日的街道。

normal.en: the root festus meant joyful, so every festival promises joy.
normal.cn: 词根 festus 本义欢乐，所以每个节日都许诺欢乐。

normal.en: harvest festival thanks the fields; spring festival welcomes the year.
normal.cn: 丰收节感谢田地，春节迎接新年。

abstract.en: A festival is a knot in time where many threads of joy are tied together.
abstract.cn: 节日是时间上的一个结，把许多欢乐的线系在一起。

abstract.en: Festivals are calendars rehearsing happiness.
abstract.cn: 节日是日历在排练幸福。

abstract.en: In festival mood, the street itself wears a costume.
abstract.cn: 节日气氛里，街道自己也穿上了盛装。

examples.en: Families gather for dinner during the Mid-Autumn Festival.
examples.cn: 中秋节期间家家户户团聚吃饭。

examples.en: Her short film won an award at the festival.
examples.cn: 她的短片在电影节上获了奖。

examples.en: The square took on a festival air with music and dancing.
examples.cn: 广场上音乐与舞蹈让整个会场充满节日气氛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饭吃我哦」—— 过节大家争着请客，饭吃我哦 → festival 节日

root: 源自拉丁语 festus「宴会的、欢乐的」，经中世纪拉丁语 festum「节日」与古法语 feste 传入英语；与 feast 同根，核心是「欢乐的固定日子」。

sensesIntro.en: From the marked celebration day to organized event series and the joyful mood itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被标记的庆祝日，到系列会演活动，再到节日的欢乐气氛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street under lanterns and flags, all roads leading to one celebration.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯笼与彩旗下的街道，条条路通向同一场欢庆。

branches.en: THE DAY: a date fixed for celebration.
branches.cn: 日子：固定的庆祝日期。

branches.en: THE PROGRAMME: a series of events and shows.
branches.cn: 节目单：连日的活动与会演。

branches.en: THE MOOD: the joy the day produces.
branches.cn: 气氛：节日带来的欢乐。

branches.en: THE TRADITION: festivals repeated year after year.
branches.cn: 传统：年年重复的节庆。

branches.en: THE STAGE: arts festivals that gather performers.
branches.cn: 舞台：聚集表演者的艺术节。

intro.en: The fest root builds a compact family of days, meals and moods.
intro.cn: fest 词根构成一个紧凑词族，覆盖日子、宴席与气氛。

latinIntro.en: Latin festus 'joyous, of a feast' feeds feast, festive and festival alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 festus「欢乐的、宴会的」同时供给 feast、festive 与 festival。
