definition_zh: 警方；警察部门；警察（人员）；维持治安；监督
definition_en: the official body that keeps public order and enforces the law, its members, and the act of keeping order in a place or process
core_image: 夜里扫过街角的蓝灯，行人自动让开一条路
scene: 深夜的街口，蓝灯在墙上扫来扫去，几个人被请到路边问话。 The police closed the road after the accident and asked drivers to turn back.
sceneCN: 这里指「警方」这个机构整体（第 1 个义项：维持公共秩序的官方部门，作主语时谓语用复数）；句意为事故之后警方封了路，让司机掉头。画面里有夜色、街口和转动的蓝灯。

pos.zh: 警方；警察部门；警察（人员）

derivatives.zh: 由 police 与 man 复合而成，义为「男警察」
由 police 与 woman 复合而成，义为「女警察」
由 police 加 -ing 构成，义为「维持治安；警务工作」

senses.title: The official body that keeps public order
senses.definition: the official organization whose members keep order, prevent crime and enforce the law, grammatically treated as plural
senses.definitionCN: 负责维持秩序、预防犯罪、执行法律的官方机构，语法上按复数处理
senses.example: The police were called when the shop alarm went off.
senses.exampleCN: 商店警报响起来时，有人报了警。
senses.why: The word first named the whole administration of a city rather than its officers, so the institution itself owns the noun, and English keeps a plural verb after it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一座城市的整套行政管理，而不是其中的警员；机构本身占住了名词，所以英语在它后面仍用复数谓语。

senses.title: The members of that body
senses.definition: the men and women who serve in that organization, counted as people rather than as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 在这个机构里任职的男男女女，按人而不是按机构来数
senses.example: Two police were standing at the gate all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 两名警察整个上午都站在门口。
senses.why: Because the noun names a body, the people inside the body are named by the same word with no plural ending, so institution and members share one form.
senses.whyCN: 名词既指一个整体，整体里的人就用同一个词来说，而且不加复数词尾，于是机构与成员共用一个形式。

senses.title: To keep order in a place
senses.definition: to keep order in an area by patrolling it and enforcing the rules there
senses.definitionCN: 在某片区域内巡逻并执行规则，从而维持秩序
senses.example: Extra officers were sent to police the square during the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 节日期间，另有警员被派去广场维持秩序。
senses.why: If the noun is the institution that keeps order, the verb is that institution set in motion over a piece of ground.
senses.whyCN: 如果名词是「维持秩序的机构」，动词就是让这个机构在一片地面上动起来。

senses.title: To control how an activity is carried out
senses.definition: to control how an agreement, system or set of rules is followed, often by a group watching its own members
senses.definitionCN: 管控某项协议、制度或规则如何被执行，常指团体自查自管
senses.example: The committee was asked to police its own spending more strictly.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会被要求更严格地管住自己的开支。
senses.why: Order has to be kept inside rules and budgets as well as on streets, so the same verb reaches from city squares into contracts and accounts.
senses.whyCN: 秩序不只在街上维持，也要在规则和预算里维持，所以这个动词从城市广场一直伸进合同与账目。

intro.en: Police goes back through French to a Latin word for the administration of a community, and its Greek ancestor is the same city word that also gave English policy.
intro.cn: police 经法语上溯到表示「共同体管理」的拉丁词，而它的希腊祖先是那个「城邦」词，英语的 policy 也出于此。

items.en: Polis meant a city and the body of citizens who belonged to it, and it supplied the whole vocabulary of civic life.
items.cn: polis 意为城邦以及属于它的公民群体，公民生活的一整套词汇都由它而来。

items.en: Politeia named citizenship and the constitution of a city, that is, the way a community was organized and governed.
items.cn: politeia 指公民身份与城邦政体，也就是一个共同体被组织和治理的方式。

items.en: Latin politia took over the sense of public administration, the running of a community as a whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语 politia 承接了「公共行政」这层意思，指把整个共同体管理起来。

items.en: Old French police meant public order and the administration that maintained it, still without any idea of a uniformed force.
items.cn: 古法语 police 指公共秩序以及维持它的行政机构，当时还没有穿制服的警队这层意思。

items.en: Modern English narrowed police to the body that keeps order and made it a plural collective; policy took the same root but drifted to a plan of action, so the two now share an origin and nothing else.
items.cn: 现代英语把 police 收窄为维持秩序的机构，并把它当作复数集体名词；policy 出于同一词根，却漂向「行动方案」，两者如今只在来源上相同，词义已不相干。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Greek city root; the near-meaning group gathers words for the people who keep order.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在希腊语「城邦」词根上的词；近义组收表示「维持秩序的人」的词。

entries.definition: A plan or course of action; it shares the Greek city root but long ago split from the meaning of public order.
entries.definitionCN: 政策；方针。与 police 同出希腊语「城邦」词根，但很早以前就从「公共秩序」这一义分叉出去了。

entries.definition: The activity of governing a country or city, from the same Greek word for the city.
entries.definitionCN: 政治；政治活动，同出那个表示城邦的希腊词。

entries.definition: The work of keeping order in an area.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一地区维持秩序的工作。

entries.definition: A male member of the police force.
entries.definitionCN: 男警察。

entries.definition: A person holding a position of authority, especially in the police.
entries.definitionCN: 担任职务、拥有权力的人，尤指警官。

entries.definition: A police officer of the lowest rank in Britain.
entries.definitionCN: 英国警衔最低的警员。

entries.definition: To move regularly through an area to watch for trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一区域定时巡查以防范问题。

entries.definition: An elected law officer in a county, chiefly in the United States.
entries.definitionCN: 郡县里经选举产生的执法官，主要见于美国。

normalIntro.en: The word is the administration of a city seen from outside: first the running of a community, then the force that keeps its order.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是从外面看到的城市管理：先是共同体的运作，后来才是维持其秩序的队伍。

normal.en: The Greek root polis means city, so police and policy are cousins that grew up in the same town.
normal.cn: 希腊词根 polis 意为城邦，所以 police 与 policy 是在同一座城里长大的表亲。

normal.en: Policy took the planning side of that root and means a course of action, while police took the order side and means the force that keeps it.
normal.cn: policy 拿走这个词根的「筹划」一侧，指行动方针；police 拿走「秩序」一侧，指维持秩序的力量。

normal.en: The police takes a plural verb because the noun names a body of people, not one person.
normal.cn: the police 后面用复数谓语，因为名词指的是一群人，而不是一个人。

normal.en: Two police without a plural ending shows that the same form can name the members as well as the institution.
normal.cn: two police 不加复数词尾，说明同一个形式既指机构，也指机构里的成员。

normal.en: Police as a verb takes an object: you police a street, a match or a treaty, because order is always kept over something.
normal.cn: police 作动词要带宾语：police a street、a match、a treaty，因为秩序总是施加在某样东西上。

abstract.en: A word for city government turning into a word for a night patrol shows how abstract administration becomes visible on a street corner.
abstract.cn: 一个指城市行政的词变成指夜间巡逻的词，说明抽象的管理最终要在街角显形。

abstract.en: Police and policy split because a community needs both a plan and someone to enforce it.
abstract.cn: police 与 policy 分家，是因为一个共同体既需要方案，也需要有人去执行。

abstract.en: The plural verb is a small grammatical trace of the idea that order is kept by many hands, not one.
abstract.cn: 那个复数谓语是一点语法痕迹，记着「秩序由许多只手维持，而不是一只」。

examples.en: The police were called when the shop alarm went off.
examples.cn: 商店警报响起来时，有人报了警。

examples.en: Two police were standing at the gate all morning.
examples.cn: 两名警察整个上午都站在门口。

examples.en: Extra officers were sent to police the square during the festival.
examples.cn: 节日期间，另有警员被派去广场维持秩序。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡利斯」——街口一有动静，警车爬坡就到，办事利索，这就是 police 的警方。

root: 希腊语 polis（城邦）→ politeia（公民身份、政体）→ 拉丁语 politia（公共行政）→ 古法语 police；与 policy 同源，但 policy 走的是「施政方案」一路，词义早已分叉。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the administration of a community; it narrows into the body that keeps order, then splits into its members and into the act of keeping order.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「共同体的管理」；它收窄为维持秩序的机构，再分出机构里的成员与维持秩序这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blue light sweeping a night street while people step aside to let order pass.
core.cn: 核心意象：蓝灯扫过夜里的街道，行人自动让开一条路。

branches.en: a blue light turning at a night corner
branches.cn: 夜里拐角处转动的蓝灯

branches.en: an officer writing a name into a notebook
branches.cn: 警员把姓名记进本子

branches.en: a line of officers walking across a square
branches.cn: 一队警员横穿广场

branches.en: a committee reading a budget line by line
branches.cn: 委员会逐行核对预算

branches.en: a station desk crowded at midnight
branches.cn: 午夜挤满人的警局值班台

intro.en: A Greek word for the city, its abstract noun of citizenship, and a Latin noun of administration hold this family together, with English splitting it into the body, the members and the task.
intro.cn: 一个希腊语的「城邦」词、它表示公民身份的抽象名词，以及一个拉丁语的管理名词，共同撑起这一族；英语再把它分成机构、成员与任务。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 结婚；嫁；娶；为……主持婚礼；使紧密结合
definition_en: to become someone's husband or wife, to take a particular person as a spouse, to conduct a wedding ceremony for a couple, or to join two things closely together
core_image: 两个人把各自的一只手放进同一只手里，一条线从此牵住两端
scene: 秋天的礼堂门口，两家人并肩站着，等那扇木门打开。 Her grandmother married a fisherman from the next village in the spring of that hard year.
sceneCN: 这里 marry 是「嫁、娶」，指与某人结成夫妻（第 1 个义项：两个人成为丈夫与妻子）；句意为那年艰难岁月的春天，她的祖母嫁给了邻村的一位渔民。图中可辨识物件：礼堂木门、并肩的两家人、等候的人群。

pos.zh: 结婚；嫁；娶；为……主持婚礼；使紧密结合

collocations.zh: 把技巧与耐心结合起来

derivatives.zh: 由古法语 mariage 而来，与 marry 同出一源，义为「婚姻；婚礼」
出自拉丁语 maritalis（婚姻的），与 marry 同源，义为「婚姻的；夫妻的」
由 marriage 加表示「可以……的」后缀 -able 构成，义为「到了可以结婚的年龄的」
由表示否定的前缀 un- 加 married 构成，义为「未婚的」

senses.title: To become husband and wife
senses.definition: to become the husband or wife of another person, or to have a wedding with someone
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人成为夫妻，或与某人举行婚礼
senses.example: They married in a small church near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一座靠海的小教堂里结了婚。
senses.why: Latin maritus named a married man and maritare named the act of taking a spouse, so the verb begins as the name of a public bond, not of a private feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maritus 指已婚的男子，动词 maritare 指娶妻或嫁人，所以这个词从一开始就是那层公开缔结的关系的名字，而不是某种私人心情。

senses.title: To take a particular person as a spouse
senses.definition: to take someone as your husband or wife, used when the partner is named as the object
senses.definitionCN: 把某个人娶为妻或嫁为夫，通常把配偶直接放在动词后面
senses.example: She married a fisherman who had never left the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 她嫁给了一个从未离开过这片海湾的渔民。
senses.why: Because the partner is the direct object, English can say who was chosen; that is why it says marry someone and not marry with someone, unlike many European languages.
senses.whyCN: 因为配偶直接做了宾语，英语就能说出被选中的人是谁；所以它说 marry someone，而不像许多欧洲语言那样加一个表示「和」的介词。

senses.title: To conduct a wedding ceremony
senses.definition: of a priest, registrar or other official, to perform the ceremony that makes two people husband and wife
senses.definitionCN: 指神职人员、登记官员或别的主持人举行仪式，使两个人成为夫妻
senses.example: The old priest had married half the couples in that valley.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老神父为山谷里半数的新人主持过婚礼。
senses.why: The same verb serves the couple and the person who declares them married, because a wedding needs an authorized voice to announce that the bond is now in force.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词既用于新人，也用于那个宣布他们成婚的人，因为婚礼需要一把被授权的嗓子说出这层关系已经生效。

senses.title: To join two things closely
senses.titleCN: 使紧密结合；使融为一体
senses.definition: to bring two things together so that they work as a single whole, said of ideas, skills or flavours
senses.definitionCN: 把两样东西凑在一起，使它们像一体那样运作，多用于想法、技艺或味道
senses.example: The chef marries smoke and citrus in a single spoonful.
senses.exampleCN: 这位厨师把烟熏味与柑橘味融进同一勺里。
senses.why: A marriage is a lasting union, so the verb stretches that image to anything deliberately put into a lasting pair, from a sauce to two crafts practised together.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻是一种长久的联合，于是这个动词把这幅画面推到任何被有意配成一对的东西上，从一味酱汁到两门一起做的手艺。

intro.en: Marry came into English from Old French in the thirteenth century, and behind it stands a Latin word for a married man; the word has always been about a bond made in public, not about romance.
intro.cn: marry 在十三世纪经古法语进入英语，背后是拉丁语里表示「已婚男子」的词；它从出现起讲的就是公开缔结的关系，而不是浪漫。

items.en: Maritus was the ordinary Latin noun for a husband and could also be an adjective for what belongs to a married man; it supplied the base of the verb.
items.cn: maritus 是拉丁语里表示丈夫的普通名词，也可作形容词指属于已婚男子的，并成为那个动词的词基。

items.en: Maritare meant to give a woman in marriage or to take a spouse, and it treated the wedding as a legal and social act rather than a mood.
items.cn: maritare 意为把女子嫁出或娶一位配偶，它把婚礼当作一件法律与社会的行为，而不是一种情绪。

items.en: Old French marier carried the same sense and supplied the form English borrowed, and its noun mariage came along with it.
items.cn: 古法语 marier 保留同样的意思，提供了英语借入的词形，名词 mariage 也随着一起传来。

items.en: Spellings such as marien and maryen settled into marry, and the verb took both the partner and the officiating priest as its object.
items.cn: marien、maryen 这类拼写后来固定为 marry，动词的宾语既可以是配偶，也可以是主持婚礼的神职人员。

items.en: Modern English keeps the wedding sense, allows both marry someone and get married, and stretches the verb to any close pairing such as flavours or skills.
items.cn: 现代英语保留婚礼义，允许 marry someone 与 get married 两种说法，并把动词延伸到任何紧密的配对，例如两种味道或两门技艺。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the wedding family and the Latin words behind it; the near group gathers verbs and nouns for taking a partner or joining two things.
note.cn: 形近组收与婚礼同族的词以及它背后的拉丁词；近义组收表示结为伴侣或把两样东西合起来的动词与名词。

entries.definition: The state or ceremony of being husband and wife, from Old French mariage.
entries.definitionCN: 夫妻的状态或婚礼；出自古法语 mariage，与 marry 同族。

entries.definition: Having a husband or wife, formed from marry with -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 有丈夫或妻子的；已婚的；由 marry 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to marriage or to a husband, from Latin maritalis.
entries.definitionCN: 与婚姻或丈夫有关的；出自拉丁语 maritalis，与 marry 同源。

entries.definition: Not having a husband or wife, formed with the negative prefix un-.
entries.definitionCN: 没有丈夫或妻子的；未婚的；由否定前缀 un- 加 married 构成。

entries.definition: To take someone as a husband or wife, or to perform a wedding; chiefly literary and older use.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人娶为妻或嫁为夫，或主持婚礼；多用于文学与较早的用法。

entries.definition: To marry someone, or to support and adopt a belief; from Latin sponsus, a promised spouse.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人结婚；也指支持并采纳某种主张；出自拉丁语 sponsus（订婚者）。

entries.definition: Two people who are married or in a romantic relationship, or to join two things together.
entries.definitionCN: 已婚或相恋的两个人；也指把两样东西连接起来。

entries.definition: To join two people or things so that they become one.
entries.definitionCN: 把两个人或两样东西结合起来，使它们成为一体。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for a married man, and its family keeps returning to the wedding, the spouse, and the lasting pair.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「已婚男子」的名词上，它的同族词反复回到婚礼、配偶与长久的一对。

normal.en: Latin maritus means a husband, so marry starts as a word about a public bond rather than a private feeling.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 maritus 意为丈夫，所以 marry 起点是一层公开的关系，而不是私人的心情。

normal.en: The verb maritare meant to give a bride or take a spouse, and English borrowed its French descendant marier.
normal.cn: 动词 maritare 意为把新娘嫁出或娶一位配偶，英语借入的是它的法语后代 marier。

normal.en: Because the partner is the direct object, English says marry someone; adding with would make it sound like a ceremony you both merely attend.
normal.cn: 因为配偶是直接宾语，英语说 marry someone；如果加一个表示「和」的介词，听起来就像一场你们只是出席的仪式。

normal.en: The priest who marries a couple uses the same word from the opposite side: he is the one who makes the bond official.
normal.cn: 为一对新人主持婚礼的神父从相反的一侧用同一个词：他是让这层关系正式生效的人。

normal.en: Marriage, marital and married all go back to the same Latin base, one as the noun, one as an adjective of the husband, one as a state.
normal.cn: marriage、marital 与 married 都回到同一个拉丁词基，一个作名词，一个作丈夫的形容词，一个表示所处的状态。

abstract.en: Two hands closing on each other, and the word names the closing, not the warmth that led to it.
abstract.cn: 两只手彼此握住，而这个词命名的是握住本身，不是通向它的那点温热。

abstract.en: A wedding is a sentence said aloud in front of witnesses, and marry is that sentence turned into a verb.
abstract.cn: 婚礼是一句在证人面前说出口的话，而 marry 就是那句话变成的动词。

abstract.en: Once a bond can be made official, it can be made between flavours or skills, and the old public vow quietly becomes a cook's trick.
abstract.cn: 一旦一种结合可以被正式认定，它也能在味道或技艺之间成立，旧日的公开誓言便悄悄变成了厨子的手法。

examples.en: They married in a small church near the coast.
examples.cn: 他们在一座靠海的小教堂里结了婚。

examples.en: The old priest had married half the couples in that valley.
examples.cn: 那位老神父为山谷里半数的新人主持过婚礼。

examples.en: The chef marries smoke and citrus in a single spoonful.
examples.cn: 这位厨师把烟熏味与柑橘味融进同一勺里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「玛丽」——婚礼上新娘被叫作玛丽，两个人从此被叫成一家人；记住 marry 是结婚，也是嫁娶。

root: 拉丁语 maritus（丈夫、已婚的）与动词 maritare 是可靠来源，经古法语 marier 进入英语；maritus 更深一层的词源一般认为与表示「年轻男子、男性」的古老词根有关，但具体来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bond publicly made; the senses then divide into the wedding itself, the named partner, the official who declares it, and any close pairing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一层公开缔结的关系；义项由此分成婚礼本身、被点明的配偶、宣布礼成的主持人，以及任何紧密的配对。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands laid into one hand, so that a single line holds both ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人把各自的一只手放进同一只手里，一条线从此牵住两端。

branches.en: two rings exchanged in a small stone church
branches.cn: 小石教堂里交换的两枚戒指

branches.en: a bride naming the fisherman she chose
branches.cn: 新娘说出自己选中的那位渔民

branches.en: an old priest raising his hand over the couple
branches.cn: 老神父在新人上方举起的手

branches.en: smoke and citrus folded into one spoonful
branches.cn: 烟熏味与柑橘味卷进同一勺

branches.en: two families standing shoulder to shoulder at a village wedding
branches.cn: 乡村婚礼上并肩站着的两家人

intro.en: A Latin noun for a husband, its verb, one French borrowing and three English endings carry marry from a wedding contract to a cook's pairing.
intro.cn: 一个表示丈夫的拉丁名词、它的动词、一次法语借入，再加三个英语词尾，把 marry 从一纸婚约带到厨子的配对。

latinIntro.en: Latin maritus and maritare are recorded and reliable, and Old French marier is the accepted bridge into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 maritus 与 maritare 有记录且可靠，古法语 marier 是被认可的进入英语的桥梁。

the married state or the wedding

definition_zh: 业余爱好；嗜好
definition_en: an activity you enjoy doing regularly in your free time
core_image: 空闲时间反复做、纯粹因为喜欢的那件事
scene: 爷爷的窗台摆满模型船，每艘都上了漆、挂了帆。 Building model ships has been his hobby for thirty years.
sceneCN: 这里 hobby 是「业余爱好」（第 1 个义项：闲暇里持续喜爱的活动）；做模型船是爷爷坚持了三十年的爱好。

derivatives.zh: hobby 加 -ist 构成，义为「爱好者； hobby 的实践者」
hobby 的复数形式
近义词，义为「消遣；娱乐」

senses.title: A regular enjoyable free-time activity
senses.definition: an activity that someone enjoys doing regularly when not working
senses.definitionCN: 工作之余经常喜欢做的活动
senses.example: Her hobby is collecting stamps from old letters.
senses.exampleCN: 她的爱好是收集旧信封上的邮票。
senses.why: Free time turns into joy when a habit is repeated for pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 闲暇因重复的乐趣变成爱好。

senses.title: A small side pursuit, not a job
senses.definition: an activity followed for pleasure, not for money or a career
senses.definitionCN: 出于乐趣而非赚钱或职业的活动
senses.example: He runs a small chess club as a hobby, not a business.
senses.exampleCN: 他办了一个小棋社，纯为爱好，不为盈利。
senses.why: Money is not the aim here; the pleasure itself pays.
senses.whyCN: 这里不图钱，乐趣本身就是回报。

intro.en: Hobby has a surprising story: it grew out of a toy horse.
intro.cn: hobby 的来历出人意料：它由「玩具木马」演变而来。

items.en: Middle English hoby was a small horse or a toy horse for children.
items.cn: 中古英语 hoby 指小马或儿童玩具木马。

items.en: The word probably came through Old French hobin, a kind of horse.
items.cn: 该词可能经古法语 hobin（一种马）传入。

items.en: Riding a hobby horse meant following a favourite pastime.
items.cn: 「骑玩具马」引申为沉迷于喜欢的消遣。

items.en: By the seventeenth century, hobby meant a favourite leisure activity.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，hobby 已指喜爱的闲暇活动。

items.en: Modern English generalised it to all regular free-time pursuits.
items.cn: 现代英语把 hobby 推广到一切固定的业余活动。

note.en: Compare hobby with its family and rivals.
note.cn: 把 hobby 与词族及近义词对照。

entries.definition: a person who has a hobby
entries.definitionCN: 爱好者，派生名词

entries.definition: more than one hobby
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，y 变 i 加 -es

entries.definition: hall or pressure group
entries.definitionCN: 大厅；游说团体，拼写音近

entries.definition: something that fills free time pleasantly
entries.definitionCN: 消遣，指打发闲暇的乐事

entries.definition: an activity you care about
entries.definitionCN: 兴趣，范围更广

entries.definition: an interest that takes over the mind
entries.definitionCN: 痴迷，程度过强、贬义色彩

normalIntro.en: Use the toy horse story.
normalIntro.cn: 用玩具马的故事记忆 hobby。

normal.en: hobby began as a toy horse you ride for fun.
normal.cn: hobby 最初是骑着玩的玩具木马——爱好也一样，图的就是乐。

normal.en: One hobby, many hobbies: y turns to i.
normal.cn: 一个 hobby，多个 hobbies：y 变 i 加 -es。

normal.en: hobbyist ends like artist and scientist.
normal.cn: hobbyist 的结尾与 artist、scientist 一样，都指人。

normal.en: A hobby fills the hours after school or work.
normal.cn: hobby 填满放学下班后的时光。

normal.en: Take up means start; give up means stop: take up a hobby.
normal.cn: take up 表开始：take up a hobby 即「培养一项爱好」。

abstract.en: Picture the smiling face of a wooden rocking horse.
abstract.cn: 想象摇摇木马微笑的脸——hobby 的童趣起源。

abstract.en: Feel the quiet joy of a room where you build things slowly.
abstract.cn: 感受在房间里慢慢做手工的安静喜悦——hobby 的味道。

abstract.en: See a shelf slowly filling with collected treasures.
abstract.cn: 看见架子被收藏的宝贝一点点填满。

examples.en: Photography started as a hobby and became her job.
examples.cn: 摄影起初只是爱好，后来成了她的工作。

examples.en: What hobbies do your classmates have after school?
examples.cn: 你的同学们放学后有哪些爱好？

examples.en: Gardening is a healthy hobby for old and young.
examples.cn: 园艺对老人和年轻人都是健康的爱好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「好癖」——「好（hào）癖就是喜欢的事」，hobby 是业余爱好。

root: hobby 源自中古英语 hoby（小马、玩具木马），可能经古法语 hobin 传入；「骑玩具马」引申为「沉迷消遣」，十七世纪起指业余爱好。

sensesIntro.en: Hobby means joy pursued freely, whether a quiet craft or a busy club.
sensesIntro.cn: hobby 指自由追求的乐趣：可以是安静的手工，也可以是热闹的社团。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a toy horse ridden purely for delight
core.cn: 核心意象：只为快乐而骑的玩具木马

branches.en: a habit of joyful free time
branches.cn: 闲暇中固定的乐趣（义项 01）

branches.en: pleasure without pay
branches.cn: 不图回报的乐趣（义项 02）

branches.en: free-time activity loved for itself
branches.cn: 因本身而被喜爱的业余活动（义项 01 · 02）

branches.en: a marker of personal taste
branches.cn: 个人趣味的标志（义项 01）

branches.en: work-free by choice
branches.cn: 自愿保持非职业属性（义项 02）

intro.en: Hobby joins person suffixes and time words easily.
intro.cn: hobby 易与人称后缀及时间词组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin otium means leisure in scholarly words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 otium 在学术词中表示闲暇。

items.meaning: a person devoted to a hobby
items.example: The hobbyist showed his bird photos.
items.exampleCN: 这位爱好者展示了他拍的鸟。

items.meaning: one who does it for love, not pay
items.example: An amateur painter won the prize.

items.meaning: a hobby as against one's job

definition_zh: 惩罚；处罚；严厉对待；粗暴使用使损坏；重创（对手）；猛烈抨击；使身体极度疲惫
definition_en: to make someone suffer for a wrong, or to treat a person or thing so harshly that it is worn down
core_image: 木槌落下，犯错的人被带离座位，去承受自己招来的那阵疼痛
scene: 夜间巡查时，看守发现一名囚犯试图翻墙逃走，于是把他单独关进一间没有窗的小屋。 The warden punished the prisoner by locking him alone in a windowless cell.
sceneCN: 这里指「因过错而使某人受苦」，对应第 1 个义项：让犯错者为自己的行为承担痛苦；句意为看守把企图逃跑的囚犯单独关进没有窗的小屋作为惩罚。画面要点：夜间走廊、翻墙的脚印、被关上的铁门；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 惩罚；处罚（及物动词，常与 for 连用说明过错）
严厉对待；粗暴使用使损坏（口语中可指物）

derivatives.zh: 由 punish 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作结果）→ 由「使人受苦这一动作」转为「所施加的那份痛苦或处罚」
由 punish 加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表能够被）→ 由「施加惩罚」转为「依法可以受罚的」
由 punish 加现在分词后缀 → 由「惩罚他人」转为形容「像惩罚一样消耗人的、折磨人的」
由 punish 加施事后缀（表施动者）→ 由「惩罚」这一动作转为「施加惩罚的那个人」
与 punish 同出拉丁 punire，加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向）→ 由「施加惩罚」转为「以惩罚为目的的、惩罚性的」
与 punish 同出拉丁 poena，经古法语形成名词 → 由「惩罚这一动作」转为「作为惩罚所付的那笔代价」

senses.title: To make someone suffer for a wrong
senses.definition: to cause a person who has done wrong to undergo pain, loss or hardship
senses.definitionCN: 使做错事的人经历痛苦、损失或艰难
senses.example: The company punished the clerk for leaking the file.
senses.exampleCN: 公司因那名职员泄露文件而惩罚了他。
senses.why: Latin punire meant to make someone pay for a wrong, so the core idea is not pain for its own sake but a debt being settled through suffering.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 punire 意为让某人为过错付出代价，所以核心并不是疼痛本身，而是一笔债通过受苦被结清。

senses.title: To sentence in a court
senses.definition: to impose a legal sentence on a convicted person
senses.definitionCN: 对已被定罪的人施加法律判决
senses.example: The court punished the fraud with five years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判处那名诈骗犯五年监禁。
senses.why: When the debt is collected by a court, the suffering is fixed by law, given a name and given a term.
senses.whyCN: 当这笔债由法庭来收取，痛苦就由法律确定，被赋予名称，也被赋予期限。

senses.title: To discipline a child or pupil
senses.definition: to correct a child or pupil by withdrawing something valued or by mild suffering
senses.definitionCN: 以收回孩子看重的某物或轻微的苦头来纠正其行为
senses.example: His parents punished him by cancelling the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 他父母取消旅行作为对他的惩罚。
senses.why: A household collects the same debt in miniature: a small wrong, a small withdrawal of what the child values.
senses.whyCN: 家庭以缩小的尺度收取同一笔债：小小的过错，配上小小地拿走孩子看重的东西。

senses.title: To treat someone with deliberate harshness
senses.titleCN: 刻意以严酷手段对待某人
senses.definition: to subject a person to prolonged harsh treatment, whether or not a rule was broken
senses.definitionCN: 使某人长时间承受严酷对待，不论是否真的违规
senses.example: The guards punished the prisoners by keeping them standing all night.
senses.exampleCN: 看守让囚犯整夜站立，以此折磨他们。
senses.why: Once pain is separated from the debt, any deliberate infliction of suffering can take the name, even where no rule exists to be broken.
senses.whyCN: 一旦疼痛与那笔债脱钩，任何刻意施加的痛苦都能叫这个名字，哪怕并不存在可供违反的规则。

senses.title: To damage something by rough use
senses.titleCN: 因粗暴使用而损坏某物
senses.definition: to wear out or damage an object by using it far harder than it was designed for
senses.definitionCN: 以远超设计承受的方式使用，使物品磨损或损坏
senses.example: Rough roads punish the tyres far more than smooth ones.
senses.exampleCN: 崎岖路面比平坦路面更伤轮胎。
senses.why: Objects cannot owe a debt, so the word transfers to rough treatment that makes a thing suffer wear, as if the thing were being made to pay.
senses.whyCN: 物品不可能欠债，于是这个词转到「粗暴对待使某物受损」上，仿佛那件东西也在被逼着付出代价。

senses.title: To defeat an opponent by a wide margin
senses.titleCN: 以压倒性优势重创对手
senses.definition: to beat an opponent so heavily that the defeat feels like a penalty
senses.definitionCN: 以极大差距击败对手，使这场失败如同一种惩罚
senses.example: The champions punished the visitors with four goals in twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军队在二十分钟内连进四球，重创了客队。
senses.why: A contest can turn a score into a debt, and a heavy defeat is that debt being collected all at once.
senses.whyCN: 比赛可以把比分变成一笔债，而一场惨败就是这笔债被一次性收走。

senses.title: To criticise sharply
senses.definition: to attack a person, work or idea with very severe public criticism
senses.definitionCN: 以极严厉的公开批评攻击某人、某作品或某观点
senses.example: The critics punished the film for its empty spectacle.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人猛烈抨击这部影片空洞的视觉堆砌。
senses.why: Words can inflict suffering too, so sharp criticism borrows the same verb and makes its target pay in reputation.
senses.whyCN: 言语也能造成痛苦，于是尖锐的批评借用了同一个动词，让对象以名声偿付。

senses.title: To exhaust the body through effort
senses.titleCN: 使身体因用力而极度疲惫
senses.definition: to strain the body so hard that the effort feels like a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 使身体承担极大负荷，让这种用力如同惩罚
senses.example: The steep climb punished legs that had not trained.
senses.exampleCN: 陡峭的山路让未经训练的腿吃尽苦头。
senses.why: The body itself can be made to pay for the effort demanded of it, so intense exertion completes the drift from moral debt to sheer physical cost.
senses.whyCN: 身体本身也能为被要求的努力付出代价，于是高强度消耗完成了从道德亏欠到纯粹身体代价的漂移。

intro.en: Punish came into English through Old French punir from Latin punire, an earlier form poenire built on poena 'penalty'. The same poena family also produced penal, penalty and punitive. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: punish 经古法语 punir 进入英语，上溯拉丁 punire，其较早形式 poenire 由 poena「罚」构成；同一个 poena 词族还生出 penal、penalty 与 punitive。年代均为约数。

items.en: The Greek noun poine named the price paid to settle a wrong, and it was borrowed into Latin as the starting point of this family.
items.cn: 希腊名词 poine 指为平息过错而付出的价，它被借入拉丁语，成为这一词族的起点。

items.en: Poena meant punishment and also the compensation that settled a wrong, and from it the verb poenire was formed.
items.cn: poena 既指处罚，也指平息过错的补偿，动词 poenire 由它构成。

items.en: Punire replaced the older poenire and meant to inflict a penalty, to avenge, to take vengeance for a wrong.
items.cn: punire 取代了较早的 poenire，意为施加处罚、报复、为过错索取代价。

items.en: Old French punir carried the Latin verb into the sense of correcting by pain, and English borrowed it around 1300.
items.cn: 古法语 punir 把这一拉丁动词带入「以痛苦纠正」的意思，英语大约在十四世纪初借入。

items.en: English punish first meant to inflict a legal penalty, then any painful correction, and finally rough handling of people or things.
items.cn: 英语 punish 最初指施加法律上的处罚，随后泛指任何带来痛苦的纠正，最后扩展到对人、对物的粗暴对待。

items.en: Punishment names the suffering as a result, punishable names what may be punished, and punitive names the intention behind a measure.
items.cn: punishment 把痛苦作为结果来命名，punishable 指可以受罚的，punitive 则指一项措施背后的惩罚意图。

note.en: The first group holds the same Latin family plus one mere look-alike; the second group offers near alternatives for the act of making someone suffer.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族的词，外加一个只是长得像的词；第二组是「使人受苦」这一动作的近义替代。

entries.definition: The noun naming the suffering imposed; the verb names the act of imposing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被施加的痛苦的名词；动词则指施加这一动作。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'liable to be punished'; it describes a legal status, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「可受处罚的」形容词；它描述的是一种法律状态，而不是动作。

entries.definition: From Latin punire with an adjective suffix; it describes the purpose of a measure rather than the deed itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 punire 加形容词后缀而来；它描述一项措施的目的，而不是行为本身。

entries.definition: Weak and small; it merely looks like punish at the start and is not related to it in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 瘦小虚弱的；只是开头与 punish 相似，并非同源。

entries.definition: To impose a penalty, usually under a written rule; it stresses the rule, while punish stresses the suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 通常依据成文规则施加处罚；它强调规则，而 punish 强调痛苦。

entries.definition: To correct behaviour through training or punishment; reform is the aim, which punish does not imply.
entries.definitionCN: 通过训练或惩罚纠正行为；改正是目的，punish 并不含此意。

entries.definition: To punish or scold severely; it often means words rather than physical suffering and sounds formal.
entries.definitionCN: 严厉惩罚或斥责；常指言语而非肉体痛苦，语体正式。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'relating to punishment'; it cannot take an object and never names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与刑罚有关的」形容词；它不能带宾语，也不指动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real derived family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的派生词族与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Punish goes back through French punir to Latin punire, and behind punire stands poena, the price of a wrong.
normal.cn: punish 经法语 punir 上溯拉丁 punire，而 punire 背后站着 poena，即过错的代价。

normal.en: The family keeps splitting the same idea: punishment is the suffering, punitive is the intention, punishable is the liability.
normal.cn: 这一词族不断拆分同一个观念：punishment 是那份痛苦，punitive 是那种意图，punishable 是那种责任。

normal.en: Punish almost always asks two questions: who suffers, and for what.
normal.cn: punish 几乎总要回答两个问题：谁受苦，以及为了什么。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the legal core: punish offenders, punish wrongdoing, be punished by law.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出法律内核：惩罚违法者、惩处不当行为、受法律制裁。

normal.en: The object can be a person, a body, a pair of shoes or an opponent, but the verb always means someone or something pays.
normal.cn: 宾语可以是人、身体、一双鞋或一个对手，但这个动词始终表示「有人或某物在偿付」。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the wrong sits on one pan and the suffering is poured onto the other until the beam levels.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一端放着过错，另一端被倒进痛苦，直到横梁齐平。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt handed to someone who never asked to buy anything.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被递给一个根本没打算买东西的人。

abstract.en: Picture a path of sharp stones laid across a field so that every step costs the walker something.
abstract.cn: 想象田野上铺着一条尖石小路，每走一步都要让行人付出点代价。

examples.en: The school punished the boys for vandalising the gym.
examples.cn: 学校因这些男孩破坏体育馆而惩罚了他们。

examples.en: Years of heavy loads had punished the truck's suspension.
examples.cn: 多年的重载已经把卡车的悬挂系统损耗得很厉害。

examples.en: The home side punished every mistake in the second half.
examples.cn: 主队在下半场抓住了每一次失误并加以重创。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕你失」——怕你失了规矩，就先让你吃一阵苦头 → 惩罚、处罚

root: 希腊 poine「为过错付出的价」→ 拉丁 poena「罚、补偿」→ 拉丁动词 poenire / punire「施罚、索偿」→ 古法语 punir → 英语 punish；同族词有 punishment、punishable、punitive、penal、penalty。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a wrong creates a debt, and suffering collects it. The collection can be a general punishment, a court sentence, a parent's correction, deliberate harshness, wear on an object, a heavy defeat, sharp criticism, or plain physical exhaustion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一条线展开：过错生出一笔债，而痛苦负责把它收回。收回的方式可以是泛指的惩罚、法庭的判决、父母的管教、刻意的严酷、对物品的损耗、一场惨败、尖锐的批评，或纯粹的身体消耗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mallet falls and the offender leaves his seat to bear the pain he brought about.
core.cn: 核心意象：木槌落下，犯错的人离开座位，去承受自己招来的那阵疼痛。

branches.en: BASE ACT: pain is deliberately dealt out because a wrong was done.
branches.cn: 基础动作：因为有人做错，痛苦被刻意施加出去。

branches.en: TWO COURTS: the debt is collected by a judge with a sentence, or by a parent with a withdrawn privilege.
branches.cn: 两种法庭：债由法官以判决收取，或由父母以收回特权收取。

branches.en: HARSHNESS WITHOUT A RULE: suffering continues even when no rule existed to be broken.
branches.cn: 无规之严：即便没有可供违反的规则，痛苦仍被继续施加。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN TARGETS: an object wears out under rough use, or an opponent is crushed by a score.
branches.cn: 非人对象：物品在粗暴使用下损耗，对手被比分碾碎。

branches.en: COST WITHOUT A VERDICT: words wound a reputation, and effort wrings out the body.
branches.cn: 无判决的代价：言语损伤名声，用力榨干身体。

intro.en: Punish sits at the head of an English family whose members split the ideas of act, result, liability and purpose.
intro.cn: punish 位于一个英语词族的首位，其成员分别承担动作、结果、责任与目的这几层意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin poena and the verb punire underlie punish, punishment, punishable and punitive, while the adjective poenalis leads to penal and penalty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena 与动词 punire 位于 punish、punishment、punishable 与 punitive 之下，而形容词 poenalis 则通向 penal 与 penalty。

items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在好几个英语词里。

definition_zh: 头痛；令人头痛的事
definition_en: a pain in the head; a problem that causes worry
core_image: 太阳穴里的小锤子：一下一下敲着同一处
scene: 他熬夜复习到凌晨，早读时太阳穴突突地跳。 He went to the nurse because of a bad headache.
sceneCN: 这里 headache 是「头痛」（第 1 个义项：头部的疼痛）；熬夜后太阳穴跳疼，headache 直接描述这种身体不适。

derivatives.zh: 头，headache 的基础词
疼痛，headache 的第二个构成成分，指持续隐痛
胃痛，同类复合词， ache 前换部位

senses.title: Pain in the head
senses.definition: a pain felt inside or around the head
senses.definitionCN: 头部内或周围的疼痛感
senses.example: Loud music gave her a splitting headache.
senses.exampleCN: 吵闹的音乐让她头痛欲裂。
senses.why: Ache means a dull continuing pain, and fixing it to the head names the commonest of all minor pains.
senses.whyCN: ache 指持续的隐痛，固定到 head 上，就命名了最常见的小病痛。

senses.title: An annoying problem
senses.definition: a problem that is difficult and worrying
senses.definitionCN: 棘手而令人烦心的问题
senses.example: The traffic jam is a real headache for drivers.
senses.exampleCN: 交通拥堵对司机来说实在令人头痛。
senses.why: A persistent worry keeps knocking like the pain keeps knocking, so trouble borrows the image of pain.
senses.whyCN: 持续烦心事像疼痛一样一下一下敲人，麻烦事由此借用疼痛的意象。

intro.en: Headache is a transparent compound built from two native words.
intro.cn: headache 是由两个本族词构成的透明复合词。

items.en: Old English had heafodece, combining head with ache.
items.cn: 古英语作 heafodece，由 head 与 ache 复合而成。

items.en: The word ache came from Old English acan, meaning to suffer continuous pain.
items.cn: ache 一词来自古英语 acan，意为「持续疼痛」。

items.en: In Middle English, headache was recorded for both the pain and, later, the figurative trouble.
items.cn: 中古英语里 headache 既记录了疼痛义，后来也有了比喻的麻烦义。

items.en: Related compounds such as toothache and stomachache formed in the same period.
items.cn: toothache、stomachache 等同类复合词也在同期形成。

items.en: Modern English kept headache as the standard word for both physical pain and daily annoyances.
items.cn: 现代英语把 headache 保留为身体疼痛与日常麻烦的标准词。

note.en: Look-alikes and pain-family neighbours.
note.cn: headache 的形近词与疼痛家族近邻。

entries.definition: emotional suffering
entries.definitionCN: 心痛；忧伤，同型复合词，部位不同

entries.definition: a severe recurring headache
entries.definitionCN: 偏头痛，特指反复发作的剧烈头痛

entries.definition: pain in a tooth
entries.definitionCN: 牙痛，同族复合词

entries.definition: a problem or difficulty

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for headache.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 headache 的五个锚点。

normal.en: head + ache
normal.cn: 结构「head + ache」（头 + 痛）字面即可读出词义。

normal.en: have a headache
normal.cn: 搭配「have a headache」（头痛）是最常见表达。

normal.en: splitting headache
normal.cn: 短语「splitting headache」（头痛欲裂）形容程度。

normal.en: toothache the same way
normal.cn: 同法记忆 toothache、stomachache：部位 + ache。

normal.en: a real headache
normal.cn: 比喻用法「a real headache」（真麻烦事）拓展词义。

abstract.en: Feel a tiny hammer tapping inside the temple.
abstract.cn: 感受太阳穴里的小锤子一下一下敲：这就是 ache 的节奏。

abstract.en: Let the tapping continue all day like a worry.
abstract.cn: 让敲击延续一整天，如同烦心事挥之不去：比喻义由此生长。

abstract.en: Swap the body part to build new words.
abstract.cn: 换掉部位就能造新词：tooth、stomach、heart + ache。

examples.en: I have a headache and want to lie down for a while.
examples.cn: 我有点头痛，想躺一会儿。

examples.en: The new tax forms are a headache for small businesses.
examples.cn: 新的报税表格让小企业头疼不已。

examples.en: A cold shower cured his headache quickly.
examples.cn: 冲了个凉水澡，他的头痛很快就好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海德爱科」——学生「海德」爱熬夜，科科熬夜就 headache（头痛）。

root: headache 由 head（头，古英语 heafod）与 ache（持续疼痛，古英语 acan）复合而成，古英语已见 heafodece 形式。同族复合词有 toothache、stomachache、backache、heartache 等，构词能产。

sensesIntro.en: From a pain in the head to a pain in daily life.
sensesIntro.cn: 从头部的疼痛到日常生活的烦忧。

core.cn: 核心意象：太阳穴里一下一下敲的小锤子

branches.cn: 头部的生理疼痛

branches.en: Problems that keep nagging

branches.cn: ache 表示的持续性隐痛

intro.cn: headache 属于 ache 复合词家族。

definition_zh: 注意；照料；关注
definition_en: careful watching or listening, or care given to someone, or public interest
core_image: 课堂上学生们抬头专心听讲
scene: 课堂上，学生们抬起头看着老师，专心地听。 Please pay attention to the teacher.
sceneCN: 这里 attention 是「注意」（第 1 个义项：专心观看或倾听）；句意为请注意听老师讲。

derivatives.zh: 参加；照料
专注的
专心地

senses.title: Careful watching or listening
senses.definition: the act of watching or listening with care
senses.definitionCN: 专心观看或倾听的行为
senses.example: Please pay attention to the teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 请注意听老师讲。
senses.why: The root means to stretch toward, and the mind stretched to one point is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为朝向伸展，心思伸向一个点就是第一义。

senses.title: Care given to someone
senses.definition: care and help given to a person who needs it
senses.definitionCN: 给予需要之人的关心与照顾
senses.example: The old man needs medical attention.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老人需要医疗照料。
senses.why: Stretching toward a person in need turns the same word from noticing into caring.
senses.whyCN: 朝有需要的人伸过去，就把这个词从「注意」变成「照料」。

senses.title: Interest shown by people
senses.definition: the interest that many people show in something
senses.definitionCN: 许多人对某事表现出的兴趣
senses.example: The new bridge attracted much attention.
senses.exampleCN: 那座新桥引起了广泛关注。
senses.why: When many minds stretch toward one thing at once, private noticing becomes public interest.
senses.whyCN: 当许多心思同时伸向一件事，私人的注意就成了公众关注。

intro.en: The recorded history of attention is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 attention 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Attendere meant to stretch toward and to give heed.
items.cn: attendere 意为向某处伸展并留心。

items.en: Attentio named the act of giving heed.
items.cn: attentio 指留心的行为。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch, the source of the middle part.
items.cn: tendere 意为伸展，是中间部分的来源。

items.en: French carried the noun into everyday use.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带入日常使用。

items.en: English used attention for careful noticing.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 attention 指专心的注意。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The verb for being present or caring.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指在场或照料。

entries.definition: The adjective for giving close attention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指专注的。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something with attention.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指专心地做某事。

entries.definition: It stresses a centre that the mind settles on.
entries.definitionCN: 强调心思集中的中心。

entries.definition: It stresses looking after a person.
entries.definitionCN: 强调照顾一个人。

entries.definition: It stresses becoming aware of something.
entries.definitionCN: 强调察觉到某物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The root means to stretch: attention is the mind stretched toward one point.
normal.cn: 词根意为伸展：attention 就是心思朝一个点伸过去。

normal.en: The same family also gives attend and attentive.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 attend 与 attentive。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase pay attention.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「注意」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of attention in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 attention 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: careful watching or listening, or care given to someone, or public interest.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「注意」时用它。

abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of attention grows from one core image: pupils raising their heads and listening closely in class.
sensesIntro.cn: attention 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：课堂上学生们抬头专心听讲。

branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：注意、专心。

branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：照料。

branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：注意、专心、照料。

definition_zh: 信任；信赖；相信；信托
definition_en: to believe that someone is honest and will not harm you, or a firm belief in a person or thing
core_image: 一个人把钥匙交到另一个人手里，手心稳稳托着
scene: 门口站着一位老人，把一串钥匙放进年轻邻居的掌心。 She trusted her neighbour with the keys to the house.
sceneCN: 这里 trust 是「信任；信赖」（第 1 个义项：相信某人诚实、不会伤害你）；句意为她把房子的钥匙交给邻居保管，信任他。钥匙放进手心的那一刻，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 trust 与 worthy 复合，义为「值得信任的」
由 trust 加 -ful 构成，义为「轻信的；信任的」
由 dis-（否定）与 trust 复合，义为「不信任」

senses.title: Believing in a person
senses.definition: to believe that someone is honest and reliable
senses.definitionCN: 相信某人诚实可靠
senses.example: She trusted her neighbour with the keys to the house.
senses.exampleCN: 她把房子的钥匙交给邻居保管，信任他。
senses.why: The old word meant firmness and comfort, and to trust someone is to rest firmly on them.
senses.whyCN: 这个古词意为牢固与安心，而信任某人就是稳稳地靠在他身上。

senses.title: The firm belief itself
senses.definition: the feeling that you can depend on someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 觉得可以依靠某人或某物的感觉
senses.example: Years of work had built trust between the two teams.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的合作在两个团队之间建立了信任。
senses.why: The verb turned into a noun, naming the steady feeling that makes trusting possible.
senses.whyCN: 动词变成名词，命名那种让信任得以发生的稳固感觉。

senses.title: Money held for others
senses.definition: a legal arrangement in which one person holds property for another
senses.definitionCN: 由一人替另一人持有财产的法律安排
senses.example: The money was left in trust for the children.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔钱被委托保管，留给孩子们。
senses.why: If you trust someone, you may hand them your property to hold, and law gave that act a formal name.
senses.whyCN: 若你信任某人，你可能会把财产交给他保管，法律给这个行为起了正式的名字。

intro.en: Trust comes from the Old Norse traust, a word for help and firm support, and it is cousin to true.
intro.cn: trust 来自古诺斯语 traust，意为帮助与坚固的支撑，与 true 同源。

items.en: The root treuwaz meant firm and loyal, shared with true and truth.
items.cn: 词根 treuwaz 意为牢固、忠实，与 true、truth 共享。

items.en: Traust named confident hope and the help that made a person feel safe.
items.cn: traust 指有把握的期望，以及使人感到安全的那种帮助。

items.en: English took trust for the feeling that someone will not fail you.
items.cn: 英语借入 trust 表示「某人不会让你失望」的感觉。

items.en: Law developed the trust, a formal arrangement for holding property.
items.cn: 法律发展出 trust，即持有财产的正式安排。

items.en: Business names such as trust bank grew from that legal use.
items.cn: trust bank 之类的商业名称都出自这一法律用法。

note.en: The first group shares the trust stem, the second holds other words about belief and confidence.
note.cn: 第一组共享 trust 词干，第二组收其他表示相信与自信的词。

entries.definition: Deserving to be trusted.
entries.definitionCN: 值得信任的

entries.definition: Relied on over a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 受信赖的

entries.definition: A lack of trust.
entries.definitionCN: 不信任

entries.definition: To accept that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 相信

entries.definition: To depend on someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 依靠

entries.definition: A firm feeling of certainty.
entries.definitionCN: 信心；信任

normalIntro.en: Trust begins like true and ends with a firm -st, the shape of a word that stands still.
normalIntro.cn: trust 以 true 的样子开头，结尾是坚硬的 -st，像个站着不动的词。

normal.en: The ending -st appears in firm words such as steadfast.
normal.cn: 结尾 -st 出现在 steadfast 这类表示稳固的词语里。

normal.en: The past form simply adds ed: trusted.
normal.cn: 过去式直接加 ed：trusted。

normal.en: Trust someone with something means put it in their hands.
normal.cn: trust someone with something 意为把它交到他手上。

normal.en: Distrust adds dis, the prefix of undoing.
normal.cn: distrust 加 dis，这是表示否定的前缀。

normal.en: A trust in law is money held for another person.
normal.cn: 法律上的 trust 是为他人保管的钱。

abstract.en: A bunch of keys placed in an open palm.
abstract.cn: 一串钥匙被放进摊开的手掌。

abstract.en: A rope tied off and held without looking.
abstract.cn: 一根系紧后不用看就握住的绳。

abstract.en: The quiet after someone says I will be there.
abstract.cn: 有人说「我会在」之后的那份安静。

examples.en: I trust her to keep the plan secret.
examples.cn: 我相信她会保守这个计划。

examples.en: Trust between the two sides took years to build.
examples.cn: 双方的信任用了几年才建立起来。

examples.en: The fund was set up in trust for the children.
examples.cn: 这笔基金以信托方式为孩子们设立。

dict_mnemonic.text: trust 与 true 同源——把心稳稳托住对方的真实，就是信任。

root: 古诺斯语 traust（帮助、坚固的支持），来自日耳曼语词根 treuwaz（牢固、忠实），与 true、truth 同源；同族词有 trustworthy、trustful、distrust。

sensesIntro.en: First the act of believing in someone, then the steady feeling itself, then the legal arrangement that feeling allows.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是相信某人的动作，再是那种稳固的感觉，最后是这种感觉所允许的法律安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: keys placed in an open palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙放进摊开的手掌。

branches.en: The person branch: believing someone will not fail.
branches.cn: 人分支：相信某人不会失信。

branches.en: The feeling branch: confidence that stays.
branches.cn: 感受分支：持续存在的信心。

branches.en: The property branch: valuables handed to another.
branches.cn: 财产分支：贵重物交到他人手里。

branches.en: The bond branch: action and feeling feed each other.
branches.cn: 纽带分支：行动与感受互相滋养。

branches.en: The paper branch: a feeling written into law.
branches.cn: 文书分支：把感情写成法律。

intro.en: Trust is a Norse free stem that English combines with worthy, -ful and the prefix dis-.
intro.cn: trust 是诺斯语来源的自由词干，英语把它与 worthy、-ful 以及前缀 dis- 组合。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Norse rather than Latin; the Latin words below express the same idea from another family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干来自诺斯语而非拉丁语；下面的拉丁词出自另一词族但表达同一概念。

items.example: The stem works as verb and noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干可作动词与名词。
它构成 trustworthy，值得信任的。

items.example: It forms trustful, full of trust.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trustful，充满信任的。

items.example: It forms trusting, ready to trust.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trusting，愿意信任的。

items.example: It forms distrust, the lack of trust.
En makes the noun into an action of handing over.
items.exampleCN: en 把名词变成交付的动作。

items.example: The ending makes a description of the past.
items.exampleCN: 词尾构成对过去状态的描述。

definition_zh: 也许；或许；可能；大概
definition_en: used to say that something may be true or may happen, or to make a suggestion, request or estimate sound softer
core_image: 一枚硬币还在空中旋转，正反两面都还握在手里
scene: 雨点敲着窗，朋友问晚上要不要出门，你还没有拿定主意。 Perhaps we should stay in and cook something simple.
sceneCN: 这里是「也许、可能」（第 1 个义项：表示不确定的可能性）；句意为也许今晚该待在家里做点简单的饭菜。

derivatives.zh: 与 perhaps 共享表示「运气、机会」的词干 hap，义为「发生；碰巧」
hap 加前缀 mis- 构成，义为「小事故；不幸」，与 perhaps 同源
hap 与 hazard 复合，义为「偶然的；杂乱的」，与 perhaps 同源

senses.title: Something may be true or may happen
senses.definition: used to say that something may be the case or may happen, without saying that it will
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事可能是真的或可能发生，但并不保证会发生
senses.example: Perhaps the train is late because of the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 也许火车是因为下雪才晚点的。
senses.why: The word began as a phrase meaning by chance, so its first job is to mark a possibility sitting between yes and no.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是「凭运气」的说法，所以它最基本的用途是标出一种停在「是」与「否」之间的可能性。

senses.title: A softened request or suggestion
senses.definition: used to make a suggestion, request or opinion sound less direct and less forceful
senses.definitionCN: 用于让建议、请求或看法听起来不那么直接、不那么强硬
senses.example: Perhaps you could send the file before Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 或许你可以在周五之前把文件发过来。
senses.why: If a claim only describes a chance, the speaker cannot be accused of pushing too hard, so the same word becomes a polite way to ask for something.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个说法只描述「有可能」，说话人就不算把话说满，于是同一个词变成了客气地提出请求的方式。

senses.title: An approximate number
senses.definition: used before a number to show that it is an estimate rather than an exact figure
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字前，表示那是估出来的数目而非精确数字
senses.example: Perhaps forty people came to the talk.
senses.exampleCN: 大概有四十个人来听了那场讲座。
senses.why: An estimate is just a possible figure rather than a measured one, which is the same hedge applied to quantity instead of to truth.
senses.whyCN: 估出来的数字只是「可能如此」的数目，而不是量出来的，这等于把同样的不确定从真假挪到了数量上。

intro.en: Perhaps is a worn-down English phrase: a Latin preposition joined to an old Norse noun for luck and written as one word.
intro.cn: perhaps 是一个磨平了的英语短语：一个拉丁语介词接上一个表示运气的古诺斯语名词，最后写成了一个词。

items.en: Latin per meant through or by, and it is still visible in phrases such as per cent.
items.cn: 拉丁语 per 意为「经由、凭」，在 per cent 这类短语里仍能看见。

items.en: Old Norse happ meant chance or good luck, and English kept it as the noun hap.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 happ 意为「机会、好运」，英语把它保留为名词 hap。

items.en: Middle English put the two together as the phrase per hap, literally by chance.
items.cn: 中古英语把两者合为短语 per hap，字面意思就是「凭运气」。

items.en: The phrase was written as one word, first as perhappes or perhapse, before the modern spelling settled.
items.cn: 这个短语被写成一个词，先作 perhappes 或 perhapse，之后才固定成现代拼写。

items.en: Modern English uses perhaps as a single adverb of possibility, while the old noun hap survives mainly inside compounds.
items.cn: 现代英语把 perhaps 当作一个表示可能性的副词，旧名词 hap 主要残留在复合词里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words sharing the old noun for luck; the near-meaning group collects adverbs that also mark possibility.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「运气」这个旧名词的词；近义组收同样标记可能性的副词。

entries.definition: An old word for chance or luck, now rare outside compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 表示机会或运气的古词，如今主要残留在复合词中。

entries.definition: To take place, especially by chance.
entries.definitionCN: 发生，尤指偶然发生。

entries.definition: Arranged without plan or order.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无计划或秩序地安排的；杂乱的。

entries.definition: A small accident or piece of bad luck.
entries.definitionCN: 小事故；不幸的意外。

entries.definition: Possibly; used to say that something may be the case.
entries.definitionCN: 也许；用于表示某事可能如此。

entries.definition: Used when something is possible but not certain.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表示有可能但不确定。

entries.definition: Used when something is more likely than not.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表示可能性较大；很可能。

entries.definition: In a way that can be imagined as possible.
entries.definitionCN: 可以想象为可能的；或许。

normalIntro.en: The word still shows its two pieces: a preposition of means and an old noun for luck.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词至今还露着两块零件：一个表示「凭借」的介词，和一个表示运气的旧名词。

normal.en: Per hap literally says by chance, which is exactly what the adverb still does.
normal.cn: per hap 字面就是「凭运气」，这正是这个副词今天仍在做的事。

normal.en: Hap is an old word for luck, and it lives on in happen, haphazard and mishap.
normal.cn: hap 是表示运气的古词，如今活在 happen、haphazard 和 mishap 里。

normal.en: Latin per means through or by, as in per cent, by the hundred.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 per 意为「经由、凭」，如 per cent 就是「按百计算」。

normal.en: Perhaps and maybe do the same job, but perhaps is the more written and more formal of the two.
normal.cn: perhaps 与 maybe 作用相同，但 perhaps 更偏书面、更正式。

normal.en: At the head of a sentence, perhaps usually softens a suggestion rather than expressing real doubt.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，perhaps 多半是在软化建议，而不是真的表示怀疑。

abstract.en: Keep the coin spinning in the air: while it turns, both faces are still possible, and that is the whole meaning.
abstract.cn: 想象那枚还在空中旋转的硬币：转着的时候正反两面都还可能，这就是这个词的全部意思。

abstract.en: A hedge is not a lie and not a promise, and perhaps is the little hedge people plant around a claim.
abstract.cn: 含糊其辞既不是撒谎也不是承诺，perhaps 就是人们在说法周围种下的一小圈篱笆。

abstract.en: The word costs the speaker almost nothing, yet it leaves room for the listener to disagree without a fight.
abstract.cn: 这个词几乎不花说话人什么代价，却给听者留出了不伤和气地反对的余地。

examples.en: Perhaps the rain will stop before we leave.
examples.cn: 也许我们出发前雨会停。

examples.en: Perhaps you should ask the manager directly.
examples.cn: 或许你该直接去问经理。

examples.en: There were perhaps twenty people in the room.
examples.cn: 房间里大概有二十个人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕哈普斯」——心里没底就怕说错，先加一句也许垫着；记住 perhaps 是或许。

root: 中古英语短语 per hap，字面义为「凭运气」；per 来自拉丁语 per（经由），hap 来自古诺斯语 happ（运气、机会），同源词还有 happen、mishap。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a possibility held open; the senses then spread to polite suggestions and to rough estimates of number.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一种悬着不定的可能性；义项由此扩展到委婉的建议和粗略的数字估计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin still spinning in the air, neither face settled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币还在空中旋转，哪一面都还没落定。

branches.en: a coin still spinning in the air
branches.cn: 还在空中旋转的硬币

branches.en: a cloud that may or may not bring rain
branches.cn: 说不准会不会下雨的云

branches.en: a note passed quietly to a colleague
branches.cn: 悄悄递给同事的一张便条

branches.en: a rough count made on the fingers
branches.cn: 用手指粗略点数

branches.en: a forecast that speaks of likely showers
branches.cn: 说可能有阵雨的天气预报

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin preposition of means and an old Norse noun for luck, written as one unit only in English.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示「凭借」的拉丁语介词和一个表示运气的古诺斯语名词拼成，只有英语把它写成了一个单位。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies only the preposition per; the noun hap is Germanic, borrowed from Old Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只提供了介词 per；名词 hap 属于日耳曼语，借自古诺斯语。
